149	    /// The Vocabulary field as the tool's `vocabulary` argument: split on
150	    /// commas, then `TranscriptOptions.keyterms` — the SAME trim, the same
151	    /// de-duplication keeping the first spelling, the same cap. `given` is
152	    /// the count before any of that, which is what the tool's own note says.
153	    static func vocabulary(from text: String) -> (given: Int, terms: [String]) {
154	        guard !text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty else {
155	            return (0, [])
156	        }
157	        let pieces = text.split(separator: ",", omittingEmptySubsequences: false).map(String.init)
158	        return (pieces.count, TranscriptOptions.keyterms(pieces))
159	    }
160	
161	    /// The tool's own cap condition (`AgentServer+CloudCaptions.swift`'s
162	    /// `cloudTranscription`), read across: a list is CUT only when more were
163	    /// given than kept AND what was kept is exactly the ceiling. A list that
164	    /// shrank because it held duplicates or blanks lost nothing, and saying
165	    /// it was capped would send somebody looking for terms they never typed.
166	    static func capNote(given: Int, kept: Int) -> String? {
167	        guard given > kept, kept == AssemblyAIClient.maxKeyterms else { return nil }
168	        return "Vocabulary was capped at \(AssemblyAIClient.maxKeyterms) terms (AssemblyAI's "
169	            + "limit); \(given) were given."
170	    }

172	    // MARK: - The estimate
173	
174	    /// One `Facts` per media of the current scope, read from disk ONCE per
175	    /// media for the life of the sheet.
176	    ///
177	    /// `refresh` runs on every keystroke in the Vocabulary field, and a stat
178	    /// of two files per media per keystroke is a spin, not a readout. What
179	    /// the facts hold cannot change under an open sheet anyway: every editor
180	    /// action validates false while one is attached.
181	    func cloudFacts(for jobs: [Transcriber.Job]) -> [CloudEstimate.Facts] {
182	        guard let cache = document?.cacheDirectory else { return [] }
183	        var order: [UInt32] = []
184	        for job in jobs where !order.contains(job.media) { order.append(job.media) }
185	        let missing = jobs.filter { cloudFactsCache[$0.media] == nil }
186	        if !missing.isEmpty {
187	            var records: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot] = [:]
188	            for entry in snapshot.media { records[entry.id] = entry }
189	            for fact in CloudEstimate.facts(
190	                jobs: missing, media: records, cacheDirectory: cache)
191	            {
192	                cloudFactsCache[fact.media] = fact
193	            }
194	        }
195	        return order.compactMap { cloudFactsCache[$0] }
196	    }
197	
198	    /// What this run would cost and why, or nil when the card is not in a
199	    /// state that can be priced — the on-device engine, or a document with
200	    /// nowhere to keep a cache.
201	    func cloudEstimate() -> CloudEstimate? {
202	        let request = runRequest()
203	        guard let options = request.options, document?.cacheDirectory != nil else { return nil }
204	        return CloudEstimate(
205	            facts: cloudFacts(for: jobs(in: scope)), options: options, refresh: request.refresh)
206	    }

210	    /// `refresh`'s cloud arm. Everything the settings state shows, recomputed
211	    /// from the controls, with nothing about a grant or an on-device model in
212	    /// it.
213	    func refreshCloud() {
214	        let jobs = self.jobs(in: scope)
215	        let estimate = cloudEstimate()
216	        let reusable = estimate?.canReuseWithoutCredential == true
217	        let hasCredential = ModelKeys.present(.assemblyAI, store: store, environment: environment)
218	        hintLabel.stringValue = !hasCredential && reusable
219	            ? "Current cached transcripts will be used without an API key or network request."
220	            : Self.hint(
221	                for: .assemblyai, region: AssemblyAIConfiguration.region(defaults: defaults))
222	        summaryLabel.stringValue = estimate
223	            .map { CloudEstimate.describe($0, fps: snapshot.canvas.fps) } ?? "Nothing to transcribe"
224	        // The WHY, where a person can reach it without it pushing the card
225	        // apart: one line per file that is not already transcribed, plus the
226	        // dated rate (R6-13 puts a held file's price on its own line).
227	        let reasons = estimate.map { CloudEstimate.reasons($0) } ?? []
228	        summaryLabel.toolTip = reasons.isEmpty ? nil : reasons.joined(separator: "\n")
229	        let note = cloudNoteText(jobs: jobs)
230	        noteLabel.stringValue = note
231	        noteLabel.isHidden = note.isEmpty
232	        let hasWork = estimate.map {
233	            !$0.uploads.isEmpty || !$0.cached.isEmpty || !$0.awaiting.isEmpty
234	        } ?? false
235	        let startEnabled =
236	            !jobs.isEmpty
237	            && document?.cacheDirectory != nil && (hasCredential ? hasWork : reusable)
238	        // CJ-12: with no key and no batch R6-16 admits, Start says which key.
239	        ModelKeys.mark(
240	            startButton, missing: !hasCredential && !reusable ? .assemblyAI : nil,
241	            enabled: startEnabled)
242	    }

244	    /// `noteText`'s cloud arm — the three things that are about the CALL and
245	    /// not about the audio: no credential, a vocabulary that was cut, and a
246	    /// scope holding nothing that can be transcribed.
247	    func cloudNoteText(jobs: [Transcriber.Job]) -> String {
248	        var notes: [String] = []
249	        if !ModelKeys.present(.assemblyAI, store: store, environment: environment),
250	            cloudEstimate()?.canReuseWithoutCredential != true
251	        {
252	            notes.append(ModelKeys.sentence(.assemblyAI))
253	        }
254	        if document?.cacheDirectory == nil {
255	            notes.append(
256	                "This project has nowhere to keep its transcript cache, so it cannot be "
257	                    + "transcribed with AssemblyAI. Save it first.")
258	        }
259	        let request = runRequest()
260	        if let cap = Self.capNote(
261	            given: request.vocabularyGiven, kept: request.options?.keytermsPrompt.count ?? 0)
262	        {
263	            notes.append(cap)
264	        }
265	        if jobs.isEmpty {
266	            notes.append(
267	                "Only a clip whose media has sound can be transcribed, and never one played in "
268	                    + "reverse.")
269	        }
270	        return notes.joined(separator: " ")
271	    }

273	    // MARK: - The run
274	
275	    /// The cloud run, on the same `CancelToken` the on-device one uses, so
276	    /// Stop cancels an upload or a wait exactly as it cancels a recognition.
277	    ///
278	    /// The transcriber is stored in `cloud` for its whole life: `run` hops
279	    /// onto its own serial queue under `[weak self]`, and a transcriber
280	    /// nobody retains never completes at all. Progress arrives on that queue
281	    /// and is hopped to main here, `ConsolidateProgressSheetController`'s
282	    /// shape and the on-device arm's.
283	    func beginCloud() {
284	        guard !didStart else { return }
285	        let request = runRequest()
286	        guard let options = request.options, let cache = document?.cacheDirectory
287	        else {
288	            NSSound.beep()
289	            return
290	        }
291	        let credential = AssemblyAIConfiguration.credential(
292	            store: store, environment: environment)
293	        var client: AssemblyAIClient?
294	        if let credential {
295	            do {
296	                let base = try AssemblyAIConfiguration.baseURL(defaults: defaults)
297	                client = AssemblyAIClient(base: base, credential: credential)
298	            } catch {
299	                // A misconfigured keyed endpoint is a result card.
300	                didStart = true
301	                showProgress()
302	                finish(.failure(error))
303	                return
304	            }
305	        }
306	        didStart = true
307	        let jobs = self.jobs(in: scope)
308	        showProgress()
309	        statusLabel.stringValue =
310	            "Transcribing \(jobs.count) clip\(jobs.count == 1 ? "" : "s") with AssemblyAI…"
311	        var records: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot] = [:]
312	        for entry in snapshot.media { records[entry.id] = entry }
313	        let run = CloudTranscriber(
314	            client: client,
315	            cacheDirectory: cache, media: records)
316	        cloud = run
317	        // A code the person NAMED comes back as itself; only an absent one
318	        // was detected, which is what makes a confidence figure honest.
319	        cloudDetected = options.languageCode == nil
320	        run.run(
321	            jobs: jobs, options: options, refresh: request.refresh,
322	            frame: max(snapshot.canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1), pages: pagesRequest, cancel: token,
323	            progress: { [weak self] fraction, name in
324	                DispatchQueue.main.async { self?.progressed(fraction, name) }
325	            },
326	            completion: { [weak self] outcome in
327	                guard let self = self else { return }
328	                self.finishCloud(outcome, report: run.report)
329	            })
330	    }
331	
332	    /// A Stop between worker success and main delivery still prevents placement.
333	    func finishCloud(
334	        _ outcome: Result<Transcriber.Outcome, any Error>, report: CloudTranscriber.Report
335	    ) {
336	        precondition(Thread.isMainThread)
337	        cloudReport = report
338	        if case .success = outcome, token.isCancelled {
339	            finish(.failure(Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled))
340	        } else {
341	            finish(outcome)
342	        }
343	    }
344	}

348	
349	/// The row under Language that installs an on-device model — spec §11 W-8,
350	/// road map 8 §5f. It shows for a supported language whose model is not on
351	/// this Mac, and while a download runs; a person presses Download, watches the
352	/// bar, and may press Cancel.
353	///
354	/// **A download is a person's act, never a tool's** (R6-12's argument read
355	/// across): this row is `SpeechEngine.download`'s only caller, and the
356	/// `transcribe` tool refuses an uninstalled locale by name instead.
357	///
358	/// **The bar is indeterminate until the download says how big it is.** W0 q3
359	/// read the request's `Progress` before any download: zero units, zero
360	/// fraction. So the row names no size and no percentage until
361	/// `totalUnitCount` is positive, and then shows the fraction.
362	///
363	/// **Both popups are LOCKED while a download runs.** Changing the language
364	/// mid-download would hide the only Cancel or show one locale's bar under
365	/// another's name, and changing the engine would repopulate Language under
366	/// it; `downloading` names the locale the running download is for and the
367	/// row reads that, never the popup. The lock is applied in
368	/// `refreshDownloadRow()`, AFTER `populateLanguages()` has set the popup's
369	/// own `isEnabled` — never inside it.
370	///
371	/// **Closing the sheet mid-download is a decision, not code**: the download
372	/// runs on in the framework, and the observation dies with this controller
373	/// (`[weak self]`).
374	extension TranscribeSheetController {
375	
376	    /// Grid row 1: an empty label cell, and the button, the bar and the
377	    /// label in one stack.
378	    func makeDownloadRow() -> [NSView] {
379	        let button = NSButton(
380	            title: "Download", target: self, action: #selector(downloadClicked(_:)))
381	        button.bezelStyle = .rounded
382	        button.controlSize = .small
383	        button.font = DS.sans(12)
384	        let bar = NSProgressIndicator()
385	        bar.style = .bar
386	        bar.controlSize = .small
387	        bar.minValue = 0
388	        bar.maxValue = 1
389	        bar.isIndeterminate = true
390	        bar.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: 80).isActive = true
391	        let label = NSTextField(labelWithString: "")
392	        label.font = DS.sans(11)
393	        label.textColor = DS.textMuted
394	        label.lineBreakMode = .byTruncatingTail
395	        downloadButton = button
396	        downloadBar = bar
397	        downloadLabel = label
398	        let stack = NSStackView(views: [button, bar, label])
399	        stack.orientation = .horizontal
400	        stack.alignment = .centerY
401	        stack.spacing = 8
402	        return [fieldLabel(""), stack]
403	    }
404	
405	    /// The row's whole state, recomputed — `refresh()` calls it last, and
406	    /// every progress hop ends in it.
407	    func refreshDownloadRow() {
408	        guard let grid = grid, let button = downloadButton, let bar = downloadBar,
409	            let label = downloadLabel
410	        else { return }
411	        let running = downloading
412	        let visible = running != nil || (engine == .apple && language?.installed == false)
413	        if grid.numberOfRows > 1 { grid.row(at: 1).isHidden = !visible }
414	        guard let running else {
415	            button.title = "Download"
416	            button.isEnabled = true
417	            bar.isHidden = true
418	            bar.stopAnimation(nil)
419	            label.stringValue = ""
420	            return
421	        }
422	        languagePopup.isEnabled = false
423	        enginePopup.isEnabled = false
424	        button.title = "Cancel"
425	        // Nothing to cancel until the request's `Progress` has arrived: a
426	        // Cancel pressed before it would do nothing and the download run on.
427	        button.isEnabled = downloadProgress != nil
428	        bar.isHidden = false
429	        var text = "Downloading \(running.displayName)…"
430	        if let progress = downloadProgress, progress.totalUnitCount > 0 {
431	            bar.stopAnimation(nil)
432	            bar.isIndeterminate = false
433	            bar.doubleValue = min(max(progress.fractionCompleted, 0), 1)
434	            text += " \(Int(progress.fractionCompleted * 100))%"
435	        } else {
436	            bar.isIndeterminate = true
437	            bar.startAnimation(nil)
438	        }
439	        label.stringValue = text
440	    }
441	
442	    /// Download when none runs; Cancel the running one otherwise.
443	    @objc func downloadClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
444	        guard downloading == nil else {
445	            downloadProgress?.cancel()
446	            return
447	        }
448	        guard engine == .apple, let chosen = language, !chosen.installed else {
449	            NSSound.beep()
450	            return
451	        }
452	        downloading = chosen
453	        refreshDownloadRow()
454	        SpeechEngine.download(
455	            chosen.locale,
456	            progress: { [weak self] progress in self?.observe(progress) },
457	            completion: { [weak self] result in self?.downloadFinished(result) })
458	    }
459	
460	    /// Holds the request's `Progress` and watches its two numbers, each
461	    /// change hopped to main and ending in `refreshDownloadRow()`.
462	    private func observe(_ progress: Progress) {
463	        downloadProgress = progress
464	        downloadObservation = progress.observe(
465	            \.fractionCompleted, options: [.new]
466	        ) { [weak self] _, _ in
467	            DispatchQueue.main.async { self?.refreshDownloadRow() }
468	        }
469	        refreshDownloadRow()
470	    }
471	
472	    /// The completion's one-line forward. The downloaded locale is captured
473	    /// BEFORE `populateLanguages()` reselects the default, and selected
474	    /// again after it. A cancel is not reported; any other failure is one
475	    /// line in the note until the next refresh.
476	    func downloadFinished(_ result: Result<Void, any Error>) {
477	        let identifier = downloading?.identifier
478	        let cancelled = downloadProgress?.isCancelled ?? false
479	        downloading = nil
480	        downloadProgress = nil
481	        downloadObservation = nil
482	        enginePopup.isEnabled = true
483	        switch result {
484	        case .success:
485	            Transcriber.forgetLanguages()
486	            languages = Transcriber.supportedLanguages()
487	            populateLanguages()
488	            if let identifier { select(languageIdentifier: identifier) }
489	            refresh()
490	        case .failure(let error):
491	            populateLanguages()
492	            if let identifier { select(languageIdentifier: identifier) }
493	            refresh()
494	            guard !cancelled, !(error is CancellationError) else { return }
495	            noteLabel.stringValue = "The download did not finish: \(error.localizedDescription)"
496	            noteLabel.isHidden = false
497	        }
498	    }
499	
500	    /// Selects the Language row whose identifier this is; a miss keeps
501	    /// whatever `populateLanguages()` chose.
502	    func select(languageIdentifier: String) {
503	        if let index = languagePopup.itemArray.firstIndex(where: {
504	            $0.representedObject as? String == languageIdentifier
505	        }) {
506	            languagePopup.selectItem(at: index)
507	        }
508	    }

512	/// AssemblyAI's published prices, dated — road map 6 §8's two rows.
513	///
514	/// They are CONSTANTS with a date beside them rather than anything the app
515	/// asks the service for, because AssemblyAI publishes no price endpoint and a
516	/// number invented at run time would be worse than a stale one nobody can
517	/// check. Everything that shows them says "at AssemblyAI's published rate",
518	/// so a figure that has gone stale reads as one.
519	enum AssemblyAIRates {
520	    /// The day the two numbers below were read off AssemblyAI's pricing page.
521	    static let readOn = "2026-09-17"
522	    /// Dollars per hour of audio for Universal-3.5 Pro.
523	    static let perHour = 0.21
524	    /// What speaker labels add, per hour.
525	    static let speakersPerHour = 0.02
526	}
527	
528	/// What a cloud caption run would cost and why — road map 6 §5e's summary
529	/// line, as a PURE value with no run, no client and no sheet in it.
530	///
531	/// **Why it is a type and not four lines inside the sheet.** The estimate is
532	/// the one thing a person sees before agreeing to spend somebody's money and
533	/// to send their audio to another company, and it has to be right about three
534	/// separate things: which files this run would upload, how much audio that is,
535	/// and what that costs. Each of those is a rule with an edge — R6-11 holds a
536	/// media whose earlier delete is unconfirmed, a cached media costs nothing, a
537	/// media whose file will not read costs nothing and transcribes nothing — so
538	/// the arithmetic is a value the probe reads over a table rather than a
539	/// summary somebody typed into a label.
540	///
541	/// **Spec §11's R6-13 is the whole of the awaiting clause.** A held media is
542	/// neither "to upload" (this run will not upload it, and quoting for it would
543	/// quote for work that is not going to happen) nor hidden (a file that
544	/// silently does not transcribe is the failure the clause exists to
545	/// prevent). It is its own count in `describe` and its own line in `reasons`,
546	/// and that line carries what it WOULD cost if the janitor clears the delete.
547	///
548	/// **One disk read, and it is not in this arithmetic.** `facts(jobs:…)` is
549	/// the only member that opens a file: it reads each media's marker, whether
550	/// the transcript itself reads back, and the janitor's list, once per media.
551	/// Everything else — `fate`, `uploadTicks`, `dollars`, `money`, `describe`,
552	/// `reasons` — is a function of those facts, so the sheet can recompute the
553	/// whole readout on every keystroke without touching the disk again.
554	struct CloudEstimate: Equatable {
555	
556	    /// Why a media is not being served from the cache.
557	    enum Reason: Equatable {
558	        /// There is no marker for it, or the transcript beside the marker
559	        /// will not read.
560	        case notCached
561	        /// There IS a transcript, of a file that has changed since.
562	        case fileChanged
563	        /// There is a transcript of this file, of a different REQUEST. The
564	        /// fields are in a fixed order — `model`, `language`, `speakers`,
565	        /// `vocabulary` — so one call's answer is the same sentence every
566	        /// time.
567	        case requestChanged([String])
568	        /// It would have been served from the cache, and Transcribe again
569	        /// was asked for.
570	        case refresh
571	    }
572	
573	    /// What this run would do with one media.
574	    enum Fate: Equatable {
575	        /// Uploaded, and why.
576	        case upload(Reason)
577	        /// Served from `cache/transcripts/`, at no cost at all.
578	        case cached
579	        /// R6-11 will hold it: an earlier remote delete is unconfirmed, so
580	        /// this run leaves it alone. The reason is what it would have been
581	        /// uploaded FOR, which is what makes its price meaningful.
582	        case awaitingDelete(Reason)
583	        /// Its media file could not be read, so nothing can be said about it.
584	        case unreadable
585	    }
586	
587	    /// Everything the disk knows about one media, read once.
588	    struct Facts: Equatable {
589	        let media: UInt32
590	        let name: String
591	        let duration: Ticks
592	        /// The file as it is NOW, or nil when it could not be read at all.
593	        let source: MediaImporter.CacheStamp?
594	        /// `cache/transcripts/<id>.complete.json`, decoded, or nil.
595	        let marker: TranscriptStamp?
596	        /// Whether `cache/transcripts/<id>.json` reads back. Both, because
597	        /// they are separate files — `MediaTranscript.isCurrent`'s rule.
598	        let cacheReads: Bool
599	        /// Whether the janitor still owes AssemblyAI a delete for it.
600	        let deleteOwed: Bool
601	    }
602	
603	    /// One media in the readout.
604	    struct Row: Equatable {
605	        let media: UInt32
606	        let name: String
607	        let duration: Ticks
608	        let fate: Fate
609	    }
610	
611	    /// In the order of each media's FIRST clip, which is the order the run
612	    /// itself works in (`CloudTranscriber.transcribe`'s `order`).
613	    let rows: [Row]
614	    /// Whether speaker labels were asked for, which is what the rate adds to.
615	    let speakers: Bool
616	
617	    init(facts: [Facts], options: TranscriptOptions, refresh: Bool) {
618	        self.rows = facts.map {
619	            Row(
620	                media: $0.media, name: $0.name, duration: $0.duration,
621	                fate: Self.fate($0, options: options, refresh: refresh))
622	        }
623	        self.speakers = options.speakerLabels
624	    }
625	
626	    // MARK: - The facts, and the ONE disk read
627	
628	    /// One `Facts` per media, in first-clip order — the only member of this
629	    /// type that opens a file.
630	    ///
631	    /// It is a static function taking a cache directory rather than anything
632	    /// holding a document, so the sheet reads it once when it opens and the
633	    /// pure arithmetic above runs on every control change.
634	    static func facts(
635	        jobs: [Transcriber.Job], media: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot], cacheDirectory: URL
636	    ) -> [Facts] {
637	        var order: [UInt32] = []
638	        var first: [UInt32: Transcriber.Job] = [:]
639	        for job in jobs where first[job.media] == nil {
640	            order.append(job.media)
641	            first[job.media] = job
642	        }
643	        let owed = Set(MediaTranscript.undeleted(in: cacheDirectory).map { $0.media })
644	        var out: [Facts] = []
645	        for id in order {
646	            guard let job = first[id] else { continue }
647	            let entry = media[id]
648	            let stamp = entry.flatMap { MediaImporter.CacheStamp.stamp(for: $0, url: job.source) }
649	            out.append(
650	                Facts(
651	                    media: id, name: entry?.name ?? job.name, duration: entry?.duration ?? 0,
652	                    source: stamp,
653	                    marker: MediaTranscript.readStamp(for: id, in: cacheDirectory),
654	                    cacheReads: MediaTranscript.read(for: id, in: cacheDirectory) != nil,
655	                    deleteOwed: owed.contains(id)))
656	        }
657	        return out
658	    }
659	
660	    // MARK: - The rules
661	
662	    /// What this run would do with one media — `CloudTranscriber.transcribe`'s
663	    /// own classification, said in the vocabulary a person reads.
664	    ///
665	    /// It is deliberately NOT shared code with the run: the run answers for
666	    /// what it did and this answers for what it would do, and a probe row
667	    /// compares the two so the day they disagree is a scored failure rather
668	    /// than a refactor nobody checked.
669	    static func fate(_ facts: Facts, options: TranscriptOptions, refresh: Bool) -> Fate {
670	        guard let source = facts.source else { return .unreadable }
671	        let wanted = TranscriptStamp(source: source, options: options)
672	        let current = facts.marker?.serves(wanted, for: .captions) == true && facts.cacheReads
673	        if current, !refresh { return .cached }
674	        let reason: Reason
675	        if current {
676	            reason = .refresh
677	        } else if facts.marker == nil || !facts.cacheReads {
678	            reason = .notCached
679	        } else if let marker = facts.marker, marker.source != wanted.source {
680	            reason = .fileChanged
681	        } else {
682	            reason = .requestChanged(changed(facts.marker, wanted))

692	        if marker.speechModels != wanted.speechModels { out.append("model") }
693	        if marker.languageCode != wanted.languageCode { out.append("language") }

703	    var awaiting: [Row] {

713	    /// The audio this run would upload, in ticks.

716	    /// SATURATES, for that constant's own reason (R6-10): a media's duration
717	    /// comes out of a `project.json` a person can hand-write, and a readout
718	    /// that trapped on one would take the sheet down with it.

722	            let bounded = min(max(row.duration, 0), Transcriber.maxSourceTicks)

737	    /// `"about $0.36"`, and `"under $0.01"` for anything above nothing that
738	    /// rounds to no cents — quoting "about $0.00" for a run that will be
739	    /// billed is the one wrong answer this function can give.
740	    ///
741	    /// Formatted POSIX, never in the person's locale: this is a dollar figure
742	    /// with a dot in it, and a comma decimal separator would read as
743	    /// thousands.

745	        guard dollars.isFinite else { return "about $0.00" }
746	        let cents = (dollars * 100).rounded()

756	
757	    /// §5e's summary line: what would be uploaded, how much audio that is,
758	    /// what it costs, and then each of the three things that cost nothing,
759	    /// named only when there are any.
760	    static func describe(_ estimate: CloudEstimate, fps: Fps) -> String {
761	        guard !estimate.rows.isEmpty else { return "Nothing to transcribe" }
762	        var parts: [String] = []
763	        let uploads = estimate.uploads.count
764	        if uploads == 0 {
765	            parts.append("Nothing to upload")
766	        } else {
767	            parts.append("\(uploads) \(files(uploads)) to upload")
768	            parts.append(
769	                ReelTime.format(estimate.uploadTicks, fps: fps, frames: false) + " of audio")
770	            parts.append(
771	                money(dollars(ticks: estimate.uploadTicks, speakers: estimate.speakers))
772	                    + " at AssemblyAI's published rate")
773	        }
774	        let cached = estimate.cached.count
775	        if cached > 0 { parts.append("\(cached) \(files(cached)) already transcribed") }
776	        let awaiting = estimate.awaiting.count
777	        if awaiting > 0 {
778	            parts.append("\(awaiting) \(files(awaiting)) waiting on an earlier delete")
779	        }
780	        let unreadable = estimate.unreadable.count
781	        if unreadable > 0 { parts.append("\(unreadable) \(files(unreadable)) could not be read") }
782	        return parts.joined(separator: " · ")
783	    }
784	
785	    private static func files(_ count: Int) -> String { count == 1 ? "file" : "files" }
786	
787	    /// One line per row that is not being served from the cache, by FILE
788	    /// NAME, and then the rate sentence.
789	    ///
790	    /// By name rather than by media id because the person chose files, not
791	    /// ids, and an id is the tool's vocabulary. R6-13: an awaiting row's line
792	    /// says what it would cost if the delete clears, so its price is never
793	    /// hidden by the count that leaves it out of the total.
794	    static func reasons(_ estimate: CloudEstimate) -> [String] {
795	        var out: [String] = []
796	        for row in estimate.rows {
797	            switch row.fate {
798	            case .cached:
799	                continue
800	            case .unreadable:
801	                out.append("“\(row.name)” could not be read, so it cannot be transcribed.")
802	            case .upload(let reason):
803	                out.append(sentence(row, reason))
804	            case .awaitingDelete(let reason):
805	                let bounded = min(max(row.duration, 0), Transcriber.maxSourceTicks)
806	                let price = money(dollars(ticks: bounded, speakers: estimate.speakers))
807	                out.append(
808	                    sentence(row, reason)
809	                        + " It is waiting on an earlier delete and will not be uploaded in this "
810	                        + "run — \(price) more if it does.")
811	            }
812	        }
813	        if !out.isEmpty { out.append(rateSentence(speakers: estimate.speakers)) }
814	        return out
815	    }
816	
817	    private static func sentence(_ row: Row, _ reason: Reason) -> String {
818	        switch reason {
819	        case .notCached:
820	            return "“\(row.name)” has not been transcribed yet."
821	        case .fileChanged:
822	            return "“\(row.name)” has changed since it was transcribed."
823	        case .requestChanged(let fields):
824	            guard !fields.isEmpty else {
825	                return "“\(row.name)” was transcribed for a different request."
826	            }
827	            return "“\(row.name)” was transcribed with a different "
828	                + fields.joined(separator: ", ") + "."
829	        case .refresh:
830	            return "“\(row.name)” is already transcribed, and Transcribe again was asked for."
831	        }
832	    }
833	
834	    /// The dated rate, in one sentence, with the speakers surcharge folded in
835	    /// when it applies — so the figure named here is the figure the total was
836	    /// computed from.
837	    static func rateSentence(speakers: Bool) -> String {
838	        let rate = AssemblyAIRates.perHour + (speakers ? AssemblyAIRates.speakersPerHour : 0)
839	        return "At AssemblyAI's published rate of $\(amount(rate)) an hour, read on "
840	            + "\(AssemblyAIRates.readOn)."
841	    }
842	}

906	/// The sheet's language popup and the tool's `language` argument: the
907	/// `Language` row, the two cached lists (`languages()`, the locales whose
908	/// model is INSTALLED on this Mac; `supportedLanguages()`, every locale the
909	/// engine names, each marked installed or not), the display-name builder
910	/// behind both, and the two lookups the callers use —
911	/// `defaultLanguage(in:)` for the popup's first selection and
912	/// `language(matching:in:)` for a tag a person or an agent typed.
913	///
914	/// Since W2 (spec §11 W-8) both lists are ASKED of `SpeechEngine`
915	/// (`supportedLocales()`, `installedLocales()`), never written down, and
916	/// every identifier is BCP-47 (`en-US`) — the engine answers `en_US`, and a
917	/// raw compare between the two spellings never matches. No transcriber is
918	/// constructed per locale here: constructing one reserves its locale against
919	/// a cap of 5 (W0 q3), so the installed SET comes from `installedLocales()`
920	/// and the one model question, `SpeechEngine.isInstalled`, is asked only for
921	/// the locale a run chose.
922	extension Transcriber {
923	
924	    // MARK: - Languages
925	
926	    /// One row of the sheet's language popup, and the vocabulary the tool's
927	    /// `language` argument speaks.
928	    struct Language: Equatable {
929	        /// A BCP-47 identifier, `en-US` — never `en_US`.
930	        let identifier: String
931	        let displayName: String
932	        /// Whether this Mac has the model. The sheet marks a row that has not
933	        /// and offers its Download row; a run refuses it.
934	        let installed: Bool
935	
936	        init(identifier: String, displayName: String, installed: Bool = true) {
937	            self.identifier = identifier
938	            self.displayName = displayName
939	            self.installed = installed
940	        }
941	
942	        var locale: Locale { Locale(identifier: identifier) }
943	    }
944	
945	    private static let languageLock = NSLock()
946	    private static var cachedLanguages: [Language]?
947	    private static var cachedSupported: [Language]?
948	
949	    /// Every locale whose model is INSTALLED on this Mac, sorted by display
950	    /// name — the rows a run can use without a download. All `installed`.
951	    ///
952	    /// Cached only when NON-empty: an empty answer is what `askBound`
953	    /// expiring looks like, and remembering it would make the feature refuse
954	    /// for the rest of the session on a Mac where it works.
955	    static func languages() -> [Language] {
956	        languageLock.lock()
957	        if let cached = cachedLanguages {
958	            languageLock.unlock()
959	            return cached
960	        }
961	        languageLock.unlock()
962	
963	        let found = named(SpeechEngine.installedLocales(), installed: nil)
964	        if !found.isEmpty {
965	            languageLock.lock()
966	            cachedLanguages = found
967	            languageLock.unlock()
968	        }
969	        return found
970	    }
971	
972	    /// Every locale the ENGINE names, model installed or not — the
973	    /// unfiltered twin of `languages()`, each row's `installed` read off the
974	    /// installed SET by BCP-47 tag.
975	    ///
976	    /// There are two lists because a caller who named a language this Mac
977	    /// could not use has one of TWO problems with two different fixes.
978	    /// `en-XX` is a tag the engine has never heard of, and the fix is to
979	    /// spell it right; `fr-FR` is a tag it knows that this Mac has no model
980	    /// for, and the fix is a person pressing Download in the sheet. Told only
981	    /// "this Mac cannot recognise it", somebody with the second problem
982	    /// retypes a tag that was right all along.
983	    ///
984	    /// Cached like its twin, and an empty answer is not cached — nor is a
985	    /// list read against an EMPTY installed set, which is what the installed
986	    /// ask expiring looks like: cached, every row would read "not installed"
987	    /// for the rest of the session.
988	    static func supportedLanguages() -> [Language] {
989	        languageLock.lock()
990	        if let cached = cachedSupported {
991	            languageLock.unlock()
992	            return cached
993	        }
994	        languageLock.unlock()
995	
996	        let installed = Set(SpeechEngine.installedLocales().map { $0.identifier(.bcp47) })
997	        let found = named(SpeechEngine.supportedLocales(), installed: installed)
998	        if !found.isEmpty, !installed.isEmpty {
999	            languageLock.lock()
1000	            cachedSupported = found
1001	            languageLock.unlock()
1002	        }
1003	        return found
1004	    }
1005	
1006	    /// Drops both caches, so the next ask reads the engine again — what the
1007	    /// sheet's Download row does once a model has been installed.
1008	    static func forgetLanguages() {
1009	        languageLock.lock()
1010	        cachedLanguages = nil
1011	        cachedSupported = nil
1012	        languageLock.unlock()
1013	    }
1014	
1015	    /// Locales as rows: tagged in BCP-47, named in this Mac's own language
1016	    /// and sorted by that NAME rather than by tag, because a person reads the
1017	    /// name — and both lists are built here so the popup and the two
1018	    /// refusals cannot spell one locale two ways. `installed` nil means every
1019	    /// row is installed; otherwise a row is installed when its tag is in it.
1020	    /// A locale listed twice under one tag is one row.
1021	    private static func named(_ locales: [Locale], installed: Set<String>?) -> [Language] {
1022	        let names = Locale.current
1023	        var seen = Set<String>()
1024	        return locales.compactMap { locale -> Language? in
1025	            let identifier = locale.identifier(.bcp47)
1026	            guard seen.insert(identifier).inserted else { return nil }
1027	            return Language(
1028	                identifier: identifier,
1029	                displayName: names.localizedString(forIdentifier: identifier) ?? identifier,
1030	                installed: installed.map { $0.contains(identifier) } ?? true)
1031	        }.sorted {
1032	            $0.displayName.localizedStandardCompare($1.displayName) == .orderedAscending
1033	        }
1034	    }
1035	
1036	    /// The language a run defaults to: this Mac's own, then anything sharing
1037	    /// its language code, then the first row — an INSTALLED row preferred at
1038	    /// each step. Compared in BCP-47 (`Locale.current.identifier` is `en_US`
1039	    /// and the rows are `en-US`). Over `languages()`, where every row is
1040	    /// installed, this is exact → prefix → first.
1041	    static func defaultLanguage(in list: [Language]) -> Language? {
1042	        let current = Locale.current.identifier(.bcp47)
1043	        func exact(_ row: Language) -> Bool {
1044	            row.identifier.caseInsensitiveCompare(current) == .orderedSame
1045	        }
1046	        if let hit = list.first(where: { exact($0) && $0.installed }) { return hit }
1047	        if let hit = list.first(where: exact) { return hit }
1048	        let code = Locale.current.language.languageCode?.identifier ?? ""
1049	        if !code.isEmpty {
1050	            func near(_ row: Language) -> Bool { row.identifier.hasPrefix(code + "-") }
1051	            if let hit = list.first(where: { near($0) && $0.installed }) { return hit }
1052	            if let hit = list.first(where: near) { return hit }
1053	        }
1054	        return list.first(where: { $0.installed }) ?? list.first
1055	    }
1056	
1057	    /// The language a caller named — `en-US`, `en`, or a display name — or nil
1058	    /// when nothing in `list` matches it.
1059	    ///
1060	    /// It is asked of BOTH lists, and that is the point: of
1061	    /// `supportedLanguages()` to tell a misspelling from a real tag, and then
1062	    /// of `languages()` to tell a real tag this Mac has a model for from one
1063	    /// it has not. Those are the tool's two language refusals, and one
1064	    /// matcher answers both so they cannot come to disagree about what
1065	    /// counts as a match.
1066	    static func language(matching name: String, in list: [Language]) -> Language? {
1067	        let wanted = name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
1068	        guard !wanted.isEmpty else { return nil }
1069	        if let exact = list.first(where: {
1070	            $0.identifier.caseInsensitiveCompare(wanted) == .orderedSame
1071	        }) { return exact }
1072	        if let named = list.first(where: {
1073	            $0.displayName.caseInsensitiveCompare(wanted) == .orderedSame
1074	        }) { return named }
1075	        // `en` should find `en-US` — a caller who names a language rather
1076	        // than a region means the one this Mac has.
1077	        let prefix = wanted.replacingOccurrences(of: "_", with: "-").lowercased()
1078	        return list.first { $0.identifier.lowercased().hasPrefix(prefix + "-") }
1079	    }
1080	}

1199	    /// reason. A marker that dropped `language_code` when the language was
1200	    /// auto would compare unequal to one written by a build that kept it.

1203	        try container.encode(source, forKey: .source)
1204	        try container.encode(provider, forKey: .provider)
1205	        try container.encode(speechModels, forKey: .speechModels)

1208	        try container.encode(keytermsPrompt, forKey: .keytermsPrompt)

116	# Captions and transcription
117	
118	Frame Job brings captions in from a SubRip file, writes them from the speech in your clips, and writes a caption track back out as `.srt` or `.vtt`. Speech is recognised either **on this Mac**, with nothing uploaded, or by **AssemblyAI** in the cloud, using your own API key. Captions come out as two-line subtitles or as large word-by-word captions in one of five styles, where each word lights up as it is said. Every caption is an ordinary text clip, so it plays in the preview, burns into an export, and can be dragged, trimmed and restyled like any other clip.
119	
120	All three commands are in the **File** menu, next to each other:
121	
122	| Command | What it does |
123	|---|---|
124	| **File ▸ Import Captions…** | Reads a SubRip (`.srt`) file onto a new caption track. |
125	| **File ▸ Generate Captions…** | Transcribes the speech in your clips onto a new caption track. |
126	| **File ▸ Export Captions…** | Writes one caption track out as SubRip (`.srt`) or WebVTT (`.vtt`). |
127	
128	None of the three has a keyboard shortcut.
129	
130	## Captions are text clips
131	
132	However a caption gets onto the timeline, it ends up as a text clip on a track of its own at the front of the stack, so it draws over everything else. That has some useful effects:
133	
134	- The preview, a rendered frame and an exported movie all show it. Burn-in needs no extra step.
135	- You can drag one to retime it, trim its edges, split it or delete it with the usual tools ([Editing](editing.md)).
136	- You can select a run of captions and restyle them together in the inspector's Clip tab, under **Text** ([Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md)).
137	- Captions are not a soft-subtitle track that a player can switch on and off. To ship a separate subtitle file, use **Export Captions…**.
138	
139	The first caption track is named **Captions**, then **Captions 2**, **Captions 3** and so on, so separate runs can be told apart in the track headers.
140	
141	Every caption time snaps to the project's frame grid, so a caption can end up to a frame shorter than its source says. Captions on one track never overlap. When a cue starts before the previous one ends, the earlier cue is cut back to meet it, and the run reports how many were shortened. A cue that would be left shorter than one frame is skipped and reported.
142	
143	The caption commands work on the timeline you have open. With a nest opened, **Import Captions…** and **Generate Captions…** put the new track at the front of that nest, and **Export Captions…** lists that nest's tracks. To caption the main timeline, close the nest first.
144	
145	A project holds at most 4,096 clips. A caption run that would go over that limit is refused before anything changes, and the message says how many more clips would fit.
146	
147	## Import a SubRip file
148	
149	Choose **File ▸ Import Captions…** and pick a `.srt` file. The open panel reads "Choose a SubRip (.srt) caption file." and accepts `.srt` and any plain-text file, so a SubRip file saved as `.txt` imports too. A `.vtt` file is not read as WebVTT. Each cue becomes one text clip in the **Caption** preset, on a new track called **Captions** (or the next free number). The import is a single undo step, **Import Captions**.
150	
151	The reader copes with the variations real caption files have:
152	
153	- a UTF-8 byte-order mark; CRLF or bare-CR line endings
154	- a missing index line above the timing line
155	- a comma or a dot before the milliseconds, the `MM:SS` and `SS` shorthands, and any number of fraction digits
156	- position settings after the end time, which are ignored
157	- `<i>`, `<b>`, `<u>` and `<font>` tags and `{\an8}`-style overrides, which are removed, plus the common HTML entities (`&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`, `'`, ` `)
158	- text in UTF-8, UTF-16, Windows-1252 or Latin-1
159	
160	The file's own line breaks are kept. Long lines also wrap inside the caption box.
161	
162	**Malformed entries are reported, not dropped silently.** If a block has no `-->` timing line, has a time that cannot be read, ends at or before its start, or has no text, it is skipped. When the import finishes, an alert lists what was skipped by line number (the first eight, then "…and N more"), along with how many captions were shortened to fit. A clean import shows no alert. A file in which no cue can be read is refused, and the message gives the first few reasons.
163	
164	*Agents:* `import_captions` (`path`, plus an optional existing `track`; reports what landed and, under `skipped`, each malformed entry by line).
165	
166	## Generate captions from speech
167	
168	Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**. The item is greyed out when nothing in the project can be transcribed. Playback pauses and the **Generate Captions** sheet opens. It is one card: you set it up, press **Generate**, and the same card becomes the progress bar. The footnote reads "captions go on a new track".
169	
170	### What can be transcribed
171	
172	A clip can be transcribed only if it plays a movie or sound file that has an audio track, its audio is switched on, and its file is present. Clips that cannot be transcribed are skipped with a reason:
173	
174	- its source is not a media file (text, shape, still, image, graphic or nest)
175	- it plays in reverse
176	- its media has no audio track
177	- its audio is switched off (for example, the picture half of a clip after Detach Audio, whose sound is on the audio-only clip below it)
178	- its media file is missing
179	- its speed ramps, and no speed map was read for it
180	- its speed or length is degenerate
181	
182	Captions follow a clip's speed. On a sped-up, slowed or speed-ramped clip, each word lands where it is heard on the timeline ([Speed](speed.md)). They keep following it afterwards: change the speed or a ramp of a clip with sound and the captions over it move with its speech in the same undo step ([Speed](speed.md#captions-follow-a-speed-change)).
183	
184	### The sheet
185	
186	| Row | What it does | Default |
187	|---|---|---|
188	| **Language** | The spoken language. With **On this Mac**, every language this Mac's recogniser supports; a language whose model is not installed reads "— not installed". With **AssemblyAI**, **Detect automatically** and then 21 languages. | On this Mac: your Mac's own language. AssemblyAI: Detect automatically. |
189	| *(Download row)* | Appears when the chosen on-device language is not installed. See below. | — |
190	| **Engine** | **On this Mac** or **AssemblyAI**. | The engine you chose last time; On this Mac the first time. |
191	| **Speakers** | AssemblyAI only. "split by speaker, coloured in Subtitles". | Off |
192	| **Vocabulary** | AssemblyAI only. Names and jargon to expect, separated by commas. | Empty |
193	| **Transcribe again** | AssemblyAI only. "ignore any cached transcript" uploads again even when a usable transcript is cached. | Off |
194	| **From** | **Selected clips**, **In/out range** or **Whole timeline**. A choice that holds nothing transcribable is greyed. **In/out range** takes every clip that overlaps the range, whole. | Selected clips if the selection holds anything transcribable, else In/out range if one is marked, else Whole timeline. |
195	| **Style** | **Subtitles** or one of the five word caption styles. See [Caption styles](#caption-styles). | The style you chose last time; Subtitles the first time. |
196	| *(looks)* | **Slide the pill**, **Fill words as spoken**, **Dim in pauses**. See [Looks](#looks-for-word-captions). | Each one as you last left it; off the first time. |
197	| *(preview)* | A sample page drawn at this canvas's size. | — |
198	| **Replace** | "existing captions" swaps out earlier caption tracks over the same clips. See [Restyle a caption track](#restyle-a-caption-track). | Off |
199	
200	The **Speakers**, **Vocabulary** and **Transcribe again** rows are hidden, not greyed, while Engine is **On this Mac**. They appear when you choose **AssemblyAI**.
201	
202	Under the grid, a summary line gives the clip count and the length of audio (for example, `3 clips · 00:04:12.000 of audio`) or "Nothing to transcribe". Under the summary is a note explaining anything that is stopping the run. **Generate** is live only when the run can go ahead.
203	
204	### On this Mac
205	
206	The hint at the top of the sheet reads: "The words are recognised ON THIS MAC and land as ordinary text clips on a track of their own, so they show in the preview and burn into an export with no further step. Nothing is uploaded."
207	
208	Each clip's own part of its media is extracted and recognised locally. There is no permission prompt and no length limit. Nothing is cached for captions on this Mac: every run, restyling included, recognises the audio again. That is free, but it takes the time again. The sheet's preview never uses on-device words.
209	
210	**Installing a language.** Speech models are installed per Mac. If you choose a language marked "— not installed", a **Download** button appears below the Language popup, and **Generate** stays greyed until the model is in. While the download runs, the row shows "Downloading *language*… N%", the button becomes **Cancel**, and the Language and Engine popups are locked. The row shows a percentage, not a size, because the size isn't known before the download starts. When it finishes, the language is installed and selected. If the download fails, the note says why. This button is the only place a model is ever downloaded.
211	
212	If this Mac's recogniser lists no language at all, the popup reads "No on-device language", and the note asks you to reopen the sheet to check again.
213	
214	### With AssemblyAI
215	
216	The hint reads: "The audio of these files is uploaded to AssemblyAI (*region*), transcribed with Universal-3.5 Pro, and deleted from AssemblyAI once the words have been read back. Nothing is uploaded until Generate is pressed." *Region* is **United States** or **European Union**, whichever is set in Settings.
217	
218	**You need** an AssemblyAI API key, saved in **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (⌘,) under **Transcription** ([below](#your-assemblyai-key)). Without one, the note reads "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription.", **Generate** is greyed (unless every file is already cached; see below) and resting the pointer on it shows the same sentence. Saving a key in Settings turns **Generate** on with the sheet still open. If no key is saved, Frame Job also accepts one from the `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` environment variable. An untitled project can be transcribed too: its transcripts are kept in a temporary folder until the project is saved, and then go into the project package.
219	
220	**What is uploaded.** The audio of every media file behind the chosen clips is uploaded, and it is the whole file, not just the parts the clips use. AssemblyAI bills for the whole file, so a long recording that you use only briefly still costs its full length. A single file longer than 10 hours is refused before anything is sent: "“*name*” is longer than AssemblyAI's 10-hour limit for one file."
221	
222	**The price, before you press Generate.** The summary line prices the run at AssemblyAI's published rate, for example:
223	
224	`2 files to upload · 01:12:30.000 of audio · about $0.25 at AssemblyAI's published rate · 1 file already transcribed`
225	
226	The rate is $0.21 an hour of audio, plus $0.02 an hour with **Speakers** on, as published on 2026-09-17. A very short run is priced "under $0.01". When every file is already cached, the line starts "Nothing to upload", for example `Nothing to upload · 2 files already transcribed`.
227	
228	Hover over the summary to see the reason for each file, such as "has not been transcribed yet", "has changed since it was transcribed", "was transcribed with a different language", "was transcribed for a different request" or "is already transcribed, and Transcribe again was asked for", followed by the rate sentence. Two other counts can appear: a file "waiting on an earlier delete", which this run will not upload, and a file that "could not be read". A waiting file's hover line gives the price it would add: "It is waiting on an earlier delete and will not be uploaded in this run — about $X more if it does."
229	
230	**The transcript cache.** Each media file's transcript is kept in the project package and reused by the next run. A file whose cached transcript matches the request (same file, model, language, Speakers and Vocabulary) is not uploaded again and costs nothing. The caption style does not count, so restyling never uploads. A transcript made for Remove Filler Words also serves Generate Captions, so that file is not uploaded or billed again. The cache is kept per media entry, so two media entries over the same file are uploaded and billed separately. When no API key is set and every file in the run already has a current transcript, the hint changes to "Current cached transcripts will be used without an API key or network request." and **Generate** works without a key. With a key set, the usual hint stays, and the summary says there is nothing to upload. To force a fresh upload anyway, tick **Transcribe again**.
231	
232	**Filler words.** AssemblyAI's words include fillers such as um, uh, hmm, mhm, uh-huh, ah, er and erm. Captions, and the sheet's preview, leave them out, so a caption reads the same whether or not its transcript has them.
233	
234	**Deletion at AssemblyAI.** Once the words have been read back, Frame Job asks AssemblyAI to delete its copy. If AssemblyAI does not confirm the delete, the result says so:
235	
236	- Normally the delete is retried at the next run that has a key for the same account and region the transcript was made in.
237	- If no key is set when that next run starts, the result says cleanup was deferred because no API key is set.
238	- If the transcript could not be kept in the project, Frame Job has no record to retry from, and the result reads "…Frame Job cannot retry deleting it automatically. Delete it in your AssemblyAI dashboard."
239	
240	While a delete is pending, that file is not uploaded again. Its current cached transcript is still used, but **Transcribe again** is refused for it until the delete goes through.
241	
242	**Speakers.** With **Speakers** ticked, a change of speaker always starts a new cue or page. In the **Subtitles** style, each speaker's cues take their own colour, in the order the speakers first appear: white, yellow, cyan, green, then round again. Speakers are counted separately for each media file.
243	
244	**Vocabulary.** Type the words and phrases to expect, such as product names, people and identifiers, separated by commas. Blank entries and repeats are dropped (the first spelling is kept), and the list is capped at 1,000 terms. If the cap cuts your list, the note says "Vocabulary was capped at 1000 terms (AssemblyAI's limit); N were given."
245	
246	**Languages.** Detect automatically, English, English (Australia), English (United Kingdom), English (United States), Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Arabic, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, Hebrew, Hindi, Japanese, Chinese, Norwegian, Swedish, Turkish and Vietnamese.
247	
248	### Progress and the result
249	
250	While a run is going, the card shows a progress bar, "Transcribing N clips…" ("…with AssemblyAI…" for the cloud), and a detail line. On this Mac, the detail is the clip being recognised. With AssemblyAI, it is the current stage: "Extracting *file*", "Uploading *file* · 12 MB of 40", "Submitting *file*", "Waiting for AssemblyAI · 35 s", "Saving *file*". **Cancel** stops the run, and closing the sheet mid-run also stops it. After Cancel, the detail line reads "Stopping…" until the run ends, and nothing is placed.
251	
252	If one file cannot be transcribed, its clips are listed with the reason, and captions from the other files are still placed. With AssemblyAI, a key that AssemblyAI refuses ends the run straight away, so no more files are uploaded.
253	
254	Placing the captions is one undo step, **Generate Captions**. A clean run closes the sheet by itself. If there is something to report, the card stays open with **Close**, saying how many captions were added on which track, how many were shortened, which clips were skipped and why, and any of these from a cloud run:
255	
256	- a file transcribed with a fallback model instead of Universal-3.5 Pro
257	- with **Detect automatically**: the language detected for each file and how confident AssemblyAI was, for example "“interview.mov”: detected Spanish (97% confidence)"
258	- a delete AssemblyAI has not confirmed, or a transcript that could not be kept in the project
259	
260	A failure shows the error on the same card.
261	
262	*Agents:* `transcribe`. It takes `clips` (the scope), `engine` (`apple`, the default, or `assemblyai`), `language` (`auto` by default with AssemblyAI), `style`, `replace`, `slide`, `fill`, `dim`, and, for AssemblyAI only, `speakers`, `vocabulary` and `refresh`, each refused by name without `engine: "assemblyai"`. It answers the cues in timeline ticks (with each word's timing for a word style) whether or not it places them, and `place: false` changes nothing at all. `replace` is refused with `subtitles` or with `place: false`; when it is given, a placed run lists the removed tracks' ids under `replaced`. The tool never remembers the sheet's engine, style or looks, and never downloads a language model. A language whose model is not installed is refused by name.
263	
264	## Subtitles
265	
266	The **Subtitles** style makes classic two-line cues, built by these rules:
267	
268	- at most two lines of at most 42 characters each
269	- at most 6 seconds per cue
270	- at least one frame between cues
271	- never two speakers in one cue
272	
273	A word too long for a line is left whole rather than hyphenated, and wraps inside the caption box.
274	
275	Each cue uses the **Caption** text preset: Source Sans 3 Regular at 3.5% of the canvas's shorter side, centred, on a 60% black backdrop, wrapping at 80% of the canvas width, with its box centred 38% of the frame height below the middle. On a canvas taller than wide (9:16, 4:5) the box sits higher, a quarter of the frame height below the middle, and on 1080 × 1920 the text is 38 px and wraps at 864 px. On a wide or square canvas nothing changed. When cues on a tall canvas wrap to more than two lines, the report after importing or generating says so: "N captions wrap to more than two lines on this canvas."
276	
277	## Caption styles
278	
279	The five word caption styles make the large, one-row captions used in shorts and reels. Instead of a cue, each clip holds a **page** of words with each word's timing, and the word being spoken is drawn the way the style says. All five are white with the spoken word marked. They are sized to the shorter side of the canvas, so a vertical and a horizontal canvas get the same text height.
280	
281	| Style | Typeface | Case | How the spoken word shows | Position |
282	|---|---|---|---|---|
283	| **Subtitles** | Source Sans 3 Regular | As written | — (two-line cues, above) | 38% of the frame height below centre; a quarter on a tall canvas |
284	| **Highlight** | Montserrat Black, black outline | UPPERCASE | Turns yellow and pops to 112% | A quarter of the frame height below centre |
285	| **Pill** | Montserrat ExtraBold | UPPERCASE | Sits on a violet pill | A quarter of the frame height below centre |
286	| **Karaoke** | Montserrat ExtraBold | As written | Words turn yellow as they are said and stay yellow; words still to come are dimmed white. Up to two lines | 28% of the frame height below centre |
287	| **Build** | Anton, black outline | UPPERCASE | Words appear one by one; the newest is yellow and pops to 115% | A quarter of the frame height below centre |
288	| **One Word** | Bebas Neue, black outline | UPPERCASE | One large word at a time, popping to 120% | 18% of the frame height below centre |
289	
290	The text is 7.5% of the shorter canvas side, and 12% for One Word. The four display faces ship inside the app under the SIL Open Font License.
291	
292	### How pages are filled
293	
294	A page is filled to the width it actually measures in its style on your canvas, not to a word count:
295	
296	- A page fills up to 86% of the canvas width, on one line (Karaoke: up to two).
297	- It ends early at a pause of 0.25 s or more, after a word ending in `.` `?` `!` or `…`, after 3 seconds on screen, or at a change of speaker. One Word pages hold one word each.
298	- A comma, semicolon or colon just before the width runs out moves the break back to it, if the page is already at least half full.
299	- A single word too wide for the frame shrinks, down to 80% of the style's size, before it wraps.
300	- A page stays up 0.5 s after its last word, or runs up to the next page when the gap is under 0.25 s, so the row does not blink between pages.
301	- Pages never run past the end of the clip they came from.
302	
303	### The preview
304	
305	The preview under the Style row shows a sample page drawn by the same renderer the canvas uses, at this canvas's proportions. It uses the first words of the first clip's cached transcript when there is one, and "This is how it looks" otherwise. A word style shows two frames, with the first word active and then the second. A ticked **Fill words as spoken** shows the fill half done, and a ticked **Slide the pill** shows the pill half-way through its slide. **Dim in pauses** is not previewed.
306	
307	## Looks for word captions
308	
309	Three checkboxes under the Style popup each add a look to a word style's pages. Each is off until you tick it, and the sheet remembers each one between runs. A box that does not apply to the chosen style is greyed out and does nothing, but keeps its tick for when you switch back.
310	
311	| Look | What it does | Works with |
312	|---|---|---|
313	| **Slide the pill** | The pill slides from the previous word to the one being said, over 0.2 s (or less when the next word comes sooner), instead of jumping. | Pill |
314	| **Fill words as spoken** | The word being said fills from left to right as it is spoken, taking at most 0.6 s. The part already said is in the highlight colour; the rest is in the upcoming colour (Karaoke's dimmed white), or not yet drawn in Build. | Highlight, Karaoke, Build |
315	| **Dim in pauses** | The page fades to half opacity during a pause of 0.25 s or more, then comes back before the next word. It also dims before the first word when that word starts late, and after the last word until the caption ends. Each fade takes 0.1 s. | All five word styles |
316	
317	With **On this Mac** chosen and a word style selected, a note under the boxes reads "On-device words rarely carry a pause; this shows mostly with AssemblyAI." The on-device recogniser stretches each word's time across the silence after it, so few pauses are long enough to dim.
318	
319	*Agents:* `transcribe`'s `slide`, `fill` and `dim`. Each is false unless given, never what the sheet last chose. `true` is refused by name with a style it would not show on, or with `place: false`; `false` is always accepted. A placed run given any of the three lists the looks that were on under `looks`.
320	
321	## Restyle a caption track
322	
323	A style is fixed when the captions are generated. To change it, generate again with **Replace** ticked:
324	
325	1. Open **File ▸ Generate Captions…** over the same clips.
326	2. Choose the new word style and looks.
327	3. Tick **Replace: existing captions**. The line under it names each track it will remove, with its caption count, for example "Replaces “Captions” (12 captions)."
328	4. Press **Generate**.
329	
330	The old tracks are removed and the new one takes their place at the front, all in one undo step. With AssemblyAI the cached transcript is reused, so nothing is uploaded and nothing is billed.
331	
332	**Replace** is live only for a word style, and only when there is a track it may replace. That means a track named **Captions** or **Captions N** that holds only text clips, each of which overlaps a clip being transcribed. Tracks outside the run's scope are left alone.
333	
334	## Re-lay captions for a new canvas
335	
336	Word captions are paged for the canvas they were made on. After you change the canvas size (on the Document tab, or an agent's `set_canvas`), choose **File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas** to page them again for the new width.
337	
338	- Every track named **Captions** or **Captions N** that holds only text clips is looked at. A track whose pages are all in one of the five word styles Frame Job makes, with its looks, is re-paged from the words its pages hold. Every correction you typed is kept, and nothing is transcribed again.
339	- Each page is re-paged inside its own clip: a page you split, trimmed or moved keeps its words where they are, and pages are never merged across clips. Words cut off by a trim stay cut off.
340	- The new pages go on a track with the same name, in the same place in the track stack, hidden and locked if the old one was.
341	- A track is **kept as placed** when it is a matte track, holds a page with no word timings (Subtitles, or a page whose word count you changed), holds a page none of whose words starts inside it, holds a page in a style Frame Job does not make, has pages in more than one style, or the new pages would not fit in the project. A sheet after the edit names each kept track and why. Nothing appears when every track was re-laid.
342	- It is one undo step, **Re-lay Captions**.
343	
344	The item is greyed out with no caption track it can re-lay, while a sheet is open, and while a recording runs. Inside a nest it works on the nest's tracks at the nest's size. **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** does the same for the vertical copy (see [Vertical versions](vertical-and-framing.md)).
345	
346	*Agents:* `relay_captions` does the same in the container `set_scope` has open. It answers the tracks re-laid (`relaid`: the new track, the track it replaced, its name, style and page count) and the tracks kept with their reasons (`kept`). With nothing it can re-lay it is refused, naming each kept track and its reason.
347	
348	## Editing captions
349	
350	Captions are text clips, so the inspector's Clip tab edits them under **Text**: Content, Font, Style, Outline, Backdrop, Box, Reveal and Presets. Select several captions to change them together.
351	
352	On a word caption page:
353	
354	- **Case.** The style's capitals come from **Text ▸ Style ▸ UPPERCASE**. Untick it to show a page as written. Case is applied when the page is drawn, so the Content box shows the words as written, and changing case never drops the word timing.
355	- **Word style colours.** There is no inspector section for a page's word style (highlight colour, pop scale, pill colour). To change them, generate again with a different style, or have an agent use `set_text`'s `word_style`.
356	- **Editing the words.** Changing the text while keeping the same number of words keeps every word's timing. Changing the number of words drops the timing, and the page then shows plainly. The Content section notes "Not timed — regenerate to time it again". The same rule holds whether you edit in the Content box or in place on the canvas (double-click the page).
357	- **Reveal.** The text reveals (typewriter, word fade, line rise) do not apply to a timed page. The Reveal section says "Word style wins; the reveal does not apply."
358	- **Trimming and splitting.** These keep each word on the speech it times. Retiming a page by dragging it moves its words with it.
359	
360	*Agents:* `set_text` edits a caption like any text clip, including a page's `words` and `word_style`. When `words` is not empty, it must have exactly one timing for each word of the content. Otherwise the edit is refused: "this text is timed word by word: N timings for M words".
361	
362	## Export captions
363	
364	Choose **File ▸ Export Captions…**. The item is greyed out unless some track holds only text clips with caption text on them. The save panel suggests *project name*`.srt` and adds two popups:
365	
366	| Control | What it does | Default |
367	|---|---|---|
368	| **Track** | Which track to write, listed as "*name* — N cues (track *id*)", front-most first. Greyed when there is only one candidate. | The front-most candidate |
369	| **Format** | **SubRip (.srt)** or **WebVTT (.vtt)**. Changing it changes the file name's extension. | SubRip (.srt) |
370	
371	Each text clip on the track becomes one cue, at the time and with the words it has now, so a caption you dragged exports where you dragged it. Empty captions are left out. Line endings become LF, and blank lines inside a caption are removed. The two formats differ only in WebVTT's `WEBVTT` header, its missing index lines, the `.` where SubRip writes `,` in timestamps, and WebVTT escaping `&`, `<` and `>`. Exporting changes nothing in the project.
372	
373	Nothing marks a track as a caption track, so any track made only of text clips can be exported, a titles track included. A word caption track is written one cue per page, with the page's words as written: the style's UPPERCASE, its word timings and its styling are not part of a `.srt` or `.vtt`.
374	
375	**Round trips are exact to the frame.** A track exported and imported again puts every cue back on the frame it came from, at every ordinary frame rate. The file itself may not match byte for byte, because import snaps times to the frame grid: at 30 fps, `00:00:04,120` comes back as `00:00:04,133`.
376	
377	*Agents:* `export_captions` (`path`, plus optional `track` and `format`). The track is never guessed: with no candidate, or more than one and no `track` given, the call is refused and the candidates are listed. A `.srt` or `.vtt` extension in `path` is replaced by the format's own, and any other extension is kept (`chart.png` becomes `chart.png.srt`).
378	
379	## Your AssemblyAI key
380	
381	The key lives in **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (⌘,), in the **Transcription** section:
382	
383	| Control | What it does |
384	|---|---|
385	| **AssemblyAI API key:** | A secure field. "Paste your key" when none is saved. A saved key shows as a fixed row of dots and is never displayed again. Press Return or **Save** to save. |
386	| **Region:** | **United States** or **European Union**: the AssemblyAI data centre your audio goes to. Default: United States. The two regions do not share transcripts, so a pending delete is retried only in the region it was made in. |
387	| **Save** | Saves the key typed in the field ("Key saved."). |
388	| **Remove** | Deletes the saved key ("Key removed."). Live only when a key is saved. |
389	| **Verify** | Makes the cheapest signed-in call to AssemblyAI with the key in the field, or the saved key, and answers "Key accepted" or AssemblyAI's reason. It reads "Checking…" while it runs, "No API key is set." with no key, and "Settings changed since this check began. Verify again." if the key or region changes mid-check. It does not transcribe or bill anything. |
390	| **Account Page** | Opens your AssemblyAI dashboard in the browser, where you get a key and see your spending. |
391	
392	The key is saved in a file only you can read (`~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/assemblyai-key`, mode `0600`), not in the Keychain, and it is never passed on the command line. Saving, removing or changing the region updates an open Generate Captions sheet straight away. The ⓘ beside the heading explains what is uploaded, what is deleted, and the published rate.
393	
394	No MCP tool can read or change the key or the region. Only a person sets them, here.
395	
396	## Limits
397	
398	- **Import reads SubRip only.** WebVTT can be exported but not imported.
399	- Captions are burned-in text clips, not a switchable subtitle stream in the exported movie.
400	- A clip played in reverse, a clip with its audio switched off, and a clip whose media is missing or silent cannot be transcribed.
401	- **On this Mac** needs the language's speech model installed from the sheet's Download row. Speakers, Vocabulary and Transcribe again are AssemblyAI only.
402	- **AssemblyAI** needs a key (unless every file is already cached), uploads and bills each whole media file, and refuses a file over 10 hours. Vocabulary is capped at 1,000 terms.
403	- Two media entries over the same file are uploaded and billed separately.
404	- Word styles mark words by their timing only. There is no keyword emphasis and no emoji.
405	- A page's word style colours and scale cannot be edited in the inspector. Generate again, or have an agent use `set_text`'s `word_style`.
406	- Speaker colours apply only to the Subtitles style.
407	- Changing the number of words on a word caption page drops its word timing. To time it again, generate again.
408	- A style cannot be switched on a placed track. Restyle by generating again with Replace.
409	- Re-lay Captions re-pages only word caption tracks in a style Frame Job makes. A Subtitles track keeps its cues as placed; generate again on the new canvas to re-wrap it.
410	
411	## For agents
412	
413	| Tool | Mirrors |
414	|---|---|
415	| `import_captions` | File ▸ Import Captions… |
416	| `transcribe` | File ▸ Generate Captions… |
417	| `export_captions` | File ▸ Export Captions… |
418	| `relay_captions` | File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas |
419	| `get_transcript` | Reads one clip's words with their timeline times, from the cached transcript or this Mac's recogniser. It never uses the network and edits nothing. Used for cutting by transcript ([Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md)). |
420	
421	In the built-in [Assistant](assistant.md), `transcribe` with `engine: "assemblyai"` is withheld, because audio leaves the Mac only when a person chooses that in the sheet. `export_captions` asks before it writes a file. The full reference is [MCP](mcp.md).
422	
423	Filler-word removal, which needs an AssemblyAI transcript made with filler words, is covered in [Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md). The Settings window as a whole is covered in [Settings](settings.md).

182	        guard let cache = document?.cacheDirectory else { return [] }
183	        var order: [UInt32] = []

189	            for fact in CloudEstimate.facts(
190	                jobs: missing, media: records, cacheDirectory: cache)
191	            {
192	                cloudFactsCache[fact.media] = fact
193	            }
194	        }
195	        return order.compactMap { cloudFactsCache[$0] }

232	        let hasWork = estimate.map {
233	            !$0.uploads.isEmpty || !$0.cached.isEmpty || !$0.awaiting.isEmpty
234	        } ?? false
235	        let startEnabled =
236	            !jobs.isEmpty
237	            && document?.cacheDirectory != nil && (hasCredential ? hasWork : reusable)
238	        // CJ-12: with no key and no batch R6-16 admits, Start says which key.
239	        ModelKeys.mark(
240	            startButton, missing: !hasCredential && !reusable ? .assemblyAI : nil,
241	            enabled: startEnabled)
242	    }

244	    /// `noteText`'s cloud arm — the three things that are about the CALL and
245	    /// not about the audio: no credential, a vocabulary that was cut, and a
246	    /// scope holding nothing that can be transcribed.
247	    func cloudNoteText(jobs: [Transcriber.Job]) -> String {
248	        var notes: [String] = []
249	        if !ModelKeys.present(.assemblyAI, store: store, environment: environment),
250	            cloudEstimate()?.canReuseWithoutCredential != true
251	        {
252	            notes.append(ModelKeys.sentence(.assemblyAI))
253	        }
254	        if document?.cacheDirectory == nil {
255	            notes.append(
256	                "This project has nowhere to keep its transcript cache, so it cannot be "
257	                    + "transcribed with AssemblyAI. Save it first.")
258	        }
259	        let request = runRequest()
260	        if let cap = Self.capNote(
261	            given: request.vocabularyGiven, kept: request.options?.keytermsPrompt.count ?? 0)
262	        {
263	            notes.append(cap)
264	        }
265	        if jobs.isEmpty {
266	            notes.append(
267	                "Only a clip whose media has sound can be transcribed, and never one played in "
268	                    + "reverse.")
269	        }
270	        return notes.joined(separator: " ")
271	    }
