56	    enum AccessError: LocalizedError, Equatable {
57	        case credentialRequired
58	
59	        var errorDescription: String? {
60	            ModelKeys.sentence(.assemblyAI)
61	        }
62	    }
63	
64	    /// The serial queue the whole run happens on — `Transcriber.work`'s
65	    /// twin, and one of the queue seams app/CLAUDE.md lists. A run is
66	    /// network-bound minutes of somebody else's compute and must never be on
67	    /// main.
68	    private let work = DispatchQueue(label: "com.kgalligan.framejob.cloud-transcribe")
69	
70	    let client: AssemblyAIClient?
71	    /// Where `cache/transcripts/` lives for this run — the document's cache
72	    /// directory, passed by value so the run holds no document.
73	    let cacheDirectory: URL
74	    /// The media records the jobs point at, by id, for the stamp.
75	    let media: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot]
76	
77	    /// What the last run said. Written only inside `transcribe`, read only
78	    /// after it returns (or after `run`'s completion has fired), which is why
79	    /// it needs no lock: one run at a time on one serial queue, and the
80	    /// caller that reads it is the caller that waited for it.
81	    private(set) var report = Report()
82	
83	    init(client: AssemblyAIClient? = nil, cacheDirectory: URL, media: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot]) {
84	        self.client = client
85	        self.cacheDirectory = cacheDirectory
86	        self.media = media
87	    }
88	
89	    /// Transcribes every job and answers on the MAIN thread —
90	    /// `Transcriber.run`'s seam, so a sheet and a semaphore-waiting tool can
91	    /// both stay synchronous. `progress` is NOT hopped: it fires on the run's
92	    /// own queue and its caller bounces it.
93	    func run(
94	        jobs: [Transcriber.Job], options: TranscriptOptions, refresh: Bool, frame: Ticks,
95	        pages: CaptionPages.Request, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken,
96	        progress: ((Double, String) -> Void)? = nil,
97	        completion: @escaping (Result<Transcriber.Outcome, any Error>) -> Void
98	    ) {
99	        work.async { [weak self] in
100	            guard let self = self else { return }
101	            let outcome = Result {
102	                try self.transcribe(
103	                    jobs, options: options, refresh: refresh, frame: frame, pages: pages,
104	                    cancel: cancel, progress: progress)
105	            }
106	            DispatchQueue.main.async { completion(outcome) }
107	        }
108	    }
109	
110	    /// `GET /v2/transcript?limit=1` on the run's OWN queue, answered on
111	    /// main — the Settings window's Verify button.
112	    ///
113	    /// Spec §11's R6-12: verify adds no queue. `work` is already one of the
114	    /// seams `app/CLAUDE.md` lists, and a second one for a single cheap
115	    /// authenticated GET would be a queue nobody could name a rule for.
116	    ///
117	    /// It captures the CLIENT and not `self`. A verify is a wait on a socket
118	    /// and the window that asked may be gone before it answers; there is
119	    /// nothing on this object for it to write, and a strong `self` would
120	    /// keep a whole transcriber alive for the duration of a button press.
121	    func verify(completion: @escaping (Result<Void, AssemblyAIClient.ClientError>) -> Void) {
122	        guard let client = self.client else {
123	            DispatchQueue.main.async {
124	                completion(.failure(.request(AccessError.credentialRequired.localizedDescription)))
125	            }
126	            return
127	        }
128	        work.async {
129	            let answer = client.verify()
130	            DispatchQueue.main.async { completion(answer) }
131	        }
132	    }
133	
134	    /// The synchronous body, road map 6 §5a. Call it off the main thread; a
135	    /// tool that already runs on the server thread calls it directly.
136	    ///
137	    /// There is no ceiling to report on the other side of a REST call, and
138	    /// since W2 there is none on this Mac either (spec §11 W-8): the tool's
139	    /// `truncated` key is gone for both engines, and the proof says so.
140	    func transcribe(
141	        _ jobs: [Transcriber.Job], options: TranscriptOptions, refresh: Bool, frame: Ticks,
142	        pages: CaptionPages.Request, cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken,
143	        progress: ((Double, String) -> Void)? = nil
144	    ) throws -> Transcriber.Outcome {
145	        report = Report()
146	        var last = 0.0
147	        func publish(_ value: Double, _ detail: String) {
148	            last = max(last, value)
149	            progress?(last, detail)
150	        }
151	        publish(0, "")
152	
153	        // (1) The janitor, FIRST on keyed runs — before anything this run does can
154	        // overwrite the file that holds an id we still owe a DELETE. A Stop
155	        // the person has ALREADY pressed is answered above it, and one that
156	        // arrives during it is heard between its items (the reader review,
157	        // §10.13 R1·2).
158	        if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
159	        if client == nil {
160	            report.janitorDeferred = MediaTranscript.undeleted(in: cacheDirectory).map(\.media)
161	        } else {
162	            let janitor = retryDeletes(cancel: cancel)
163	            report.janitorDeleted = janitor.deleted
164	            report.janitorFailed = janitor.failed
165	        }
166	        if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
167	        if client == nil, jobs.isEmpty || refresh { throw AccessError.credentialRequired }
168	
169	        // (2) Grouped by media, in the order of each media's FIRST clip, and
170	        // classified before any work starts so the progress shares are known.
171	        var order: [UInt32] = []
172	        var grouped: [UInt32: [Transcriber.Job]] = [:]
173	        for job in jobs {
174	            if grouped[job.media] == nil { order.append(job.media) }
175	            grouped[job.media, default: []].append(job)
176	        }
177	        // Admit the entire keyless batch from disk before deriving a cue.
178	        // Holding these decoded files also closes the gap between admission
179	        // and use if a package file disappears while the worker is running.
180	        var keylessFiles: [UInt32: MediaTranscript.File] = [:]
181	        if client == nil {
182	            for id in order {
183	                if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
184	                guard let entry = media[id], let url = grouped[id]?.first?.source,
185	                    let source = MediaImporter.CacheStamp.stamp(for: entry, url: url),
186	                    MediaTranscript.readStamp(for: id, in: cacheDirectory)?.serves(
187	                        TranscriptStamp(source: source, options: options), for: .captions) == true,
188	                    let file = MediaTranscript.read(for: id, in: cacheDirectory)
189	                else { throw AccessError.credentialRequired }
190	                keylessFiles[id] = file
191	            }
192	            report.cached = order
193	        }
194	        var stamps: [UInt32: TranscriptStamp] = [:]
195	        var unreadable: [UInt32] = []
196	        var toUpload: [UInt32] = []
197	        var held: [UInt32] = []
198	        var cached: [UInt32] = []
199	        for id in order {
200	            if client == nil { continue }
201	            guard let entry = media[id], let url = grouped[id]?.first?.source,
202	                let source = MediaImporter.CacheStamp.stamp(for: entry, url: url)
203	            else {
204	                unreadable.append(id)
205	                continue
206	            }
207	            let stamp = TranscriptStamp(source: source, options: options)
208	            stamps[id] = stamp
209	            if MediaTranscript.isCurrent(stamp, for: id, in: cacheDirectory), !refresh {
210	                cached.append(id)
211	            } else if report.janitorFailed.contains(id) {
212	                held.append(id)
213	            } else {
214	                toUpload.append(id)
215	            }
216	        }
217	        report.held = held
218	        // Held and cached media are NOT in the shares: neither costs a
219	        // second of work, and a slice for one would make the bar stall.
220	        let bar = CloudProgress(seconds: toUpload.map { ReelTime.seconds(media[$0]?.duration ?? 0) })
221	
222	        var files: [UInt32: MediaTranscript.File] = [:]
223	        var cues: [CaptionLayout.Cue] = []
224	        var problems: [CaptionLayout.Problem] = []
225	        var clips: [UInt32] = []
226	        // Kept apart from `problems` for `Transcriber.transcribe`'s reason:
227	        // they decide WHICH refusal an empty run earns.
228	        var failures: [String] = []
229	
230	        func refuse(_ id: UInt32, _ reason: String) {
231	            for job in grouped[id] ?? [] {
232	                problems.append(CaptionLayout.Problem(tag: "clip \(job.clip)", reason: reason))
233	                failures.append("clip \(job.clip): \(reason)")
234	            }
235	        }
236	
237	        for id in order {
238	            if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
239	            if let file = keylessFiles[id] {
240	                files[id] = file
241	            } else if unreadable.contains(id) {
242	                refuse(id, "its media file could not be read")
243	            } else if cached.contains(id) {
244	                if let file = MediaTranscript.read(for: id, in: cacheDirectory) {
245	                    files[id] = file
246	                    report.cached.append(id)
247	                } else {
248	                    refuse(id, "its cached transcript could not be read")
249	                }
250	            } else if held.contains(id) {
251	                // R6-11, the whole of it: no fetch, no write, one sentence
252	                // per clip, and the file left byte for byte.
253	                refuse(
254	                    id,
255	                    "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting its earlier transcript, so it was "
256	                        + "not uploaded again; the next run with an API key retries the delete")
257	            } else if let index = toUpload.firstIndex(of: id), let entry = media[id],
258	                let url = grouped[id]?.first?.source, let stamp = stamps[id]
259	            {
260	                do {
261	                    let answer = try fetch(
262	                        media: entry, url: url, stamp: stamp, options: options, cancel: cancel,
263	                        progress: { phase, within, detail in
264	                            publish(bar.fraction(media: index, phase: phase, within: within), detail)
265	                        })
266	                    files[id] = answer.file
267	                    report.uploaded.append(answer.uploaded)
268	                    publish(
269	                        bar.fraction(media: index, phase: .saving, within: 1),
270	                        CloudProgress.detail(.saving, file: entry.name))
271	                } catch {
272	                    // R6-20: a transcript refused after it was made, whose
273	                    // DELETE failed, is owed with no file to retry it from;
274	                    // everything below reads the refusal's own `ClientError`.
275	                    let refusal = error as? AssemblyAIClient.Refusal
276	                    if refusal?.deletion == .failed { report.refusedUndeleted.append(id) }
277	                    let error: any Error = refusal?.failure ?? error
278	                    if let client = error as? AssemblyAIClient.ClientError,
279	                        case .submissionUnresolved(let authenticationStatus) = client,
280	                        cancel.isCancelled || authenticationStatus != nil
281	                    {
282	                        throw client
283	                    }
284	                    if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
285	                    if let client = error as? AssemblyAIClient.ClientError {
286	                        if client == .cancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
287	                        // An auth failure ends the run at once: every later
288	                        // media would fail the same way and each costs an
289	                        // upload to find out.
290	                        if case .keyRefused = client { throw error }
291	                    }
292	                    if let native = error as? Transcriber.TranscribeError, native == .cancelled {
293	                        throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled
294	                    }
295	                    refuse(id, error.localizedDescription)
296	                }
297	            }
298	
299	            // (4) Every job on this media, derived from the one transcript.
300	            guard let file = files[id] else { continue }
301	            for job in grouped[id] ?? [] {
302	                let words = MediaTranscript.captionWords(for: job, in: file)
303	                    .filter { $0.start < job.start + job.duration }
304	                cues.append(
305	                    contentsOf: CaptionPages.cues(
306	                        from: words, span: job.span, frame: frame, request: pages,
307	                        engine: .assemblyai, clip: job.clip, media: job.media))
308	                if words.isEmpty {
309	                    problems.append(
310	                        CaptionLayout.Problem(
311	                            tag: "clip \(job.clip)", reason: "no speech was recognised in it"))
312	                } else {
313	                    clips.append(job.clip)
314	                }
315	            }
316	        }
317	
318	        if cancel.isCancelled { throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.cancelled }
319	        guard !cues.isEmpty else {
320	            // `Transcriber.transcribe`'s two closing throws, same rule: "no
321	            // speech was recognised" is a claim about the AUDIO, and making
322	            // it when the audio was never read would send somebody looking
323	            // for words that are on the timeline.
324	            guard failures.isEmpty else {
325	                throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.failed(
326	                    failures.prefix(3).joined(separator: "; "))
327	            }
328	            throw Transcriber.TranscribeError.nothingRecognized
329	        }
330	        publish(1, "")
331	        return Transcriber.Outcome(cues: cues, problems: problems, clips: clips)
332	    }
333	}

336	/// The two halves of a cloud run that are about ONE media file: the janitor,
337	/// which is the run's first act, and the round trip, which is everything
338	/// between "this media is not cached" and "its words are on disk".
339	///
340	/// They are here rather than in `CloudTranscriber.swift` because that file
341	/// holds the run's SHAPE — the janitor, the grouping, the classification, the
342	/// per-job derivation and the two closing throws — and a reader following
343	/// that shape does not need the header's twelve fields or the order of the
344	/// five calls in front of them. Both files are under the 400-line cap a new
345	/// file has (app/CLAUDE.md, road map 6 §5h).
346	extension CloudTranscriber {
347	
348	    /// Why one media could not be sent, in a sentence with no prefix on it.
349	    ///
350	    /// `Transcriber.TranscribeError.failed` would wrap this in "The
351	    /// transcription failed: ", which is true of the run and not of the
352	    /// media, and the refusal has to name the FILE and the limit — road map
353	    /// 6 §5g puts the ten-hour refusal above the network for exactly that
354	    /// reason: it is knowable before a byte is extracted, let alone sent.
355	    enum MediaError: LocalizedError, Equatable {
356	        case tooLong(String)
357	
358	        var errorDescription: String? {
359	            switch self {
360	            case .tooLong(let name):
361	                return "“\(name)” is longer than AssemblyAI's 10-hour limit for one file."
362	            }
363	        }
364	    }
365	
366	    // MARK: - The janitor
367	
368	    /// R6-4's first act: every cached transcript whose remote copy this app
369	    /// has not managed to delete gets its DELETE retried, best effort, on
370	    /// `deleteTimeout` each.
371	    ///
372	    /// A success rewrites that one flag and nothing else —
373	    /// `MediaTranscript.File`'s header is mutated and written back through
374	    /// the same door, so the served `words` bytes are spliced through
375	    /// untouched and the file is never re-serialised. A failure is REPORTED
376	    /// rather than swallowed, because R6-11 makes it mean something: the run
377	    /// will not fetch that media at all, since this file is the one record of
378	    /// the id still owed a delete.
379	    ///
380	    /// A repeat DELETE of an already-deleted transcript answers 200 (C0's
381	    /// q6), so a retry can never make things worse.
382	    ///
383	    /// **A Stop is heard BETWEEN items.** `cancel` is optional and defaulted
384	    /// so `retryDeletes()` still means what it always did, but a run that has
385	    /// one hands its token over: each DELETE has only `deleteTimeout` of its
386	    /// own, and a cache owing three of them against a server that answers
387	    /// nothing made a person wait out fifteen seconds of a Stop they had
388	    /// already pressed (the reader review, §10.13 R1·2). What is left
389	    /// unvisited is in NEITHER list — nothing was attempted for it — which is
390	    /// safe because the one caller throws `cancelled` on the next line. The
391	    /// one IN FLIGHT is bounded rather than cut: its DELETE reads the token
392	    /// as a Stop and ends `deleteAfterStop` after it, a cut one `failed` and
393	    /// so owed like any other — kept in its file and in `janitorFailed`
394	    /// (R6-19).
395	    func retryDeletes(cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken? = nil) -> (
396	        deleted: [UInt32], failed: [UInt32]
397	    ) {
398	        guard let client else { return ([], []) }
399	        var deleted: [UInt32] = []
400	        var failed: [UInt32] = []
401	        for row in MediaTranscript.undeleted(in: cacheDirectory) {
402	            if cancel?.isCancelled == true { break }
403	            switch client.delete(id: row.transcriptID, cancel: cancel) {
404	            case .failed:
405	                failed.append(row.media)
406	                continue
407	            // An id no request could be made from is in NEITHER list: saying
408	            // `deleted` would report a delete nothing sent and would write
409	            // `remote_deleted: true` over the one record that something is
410	            // owed, and saying `failed` would HOLD the media for ever over a
411	            // string (the reader review's fix pass, §10.13).
412	            case .notSent:
413	                continue
414	            case .deleted:
415	                break
416	            }
417	            if var file = MediaTranscript.read(for: row.media, in: cacheDirectory) {
418	                file.header.remoteDeleted = true
419	                MediaTranscript.write(file, for: row.media, in: cacheDirectory)
420	            }
421	            deleted.append(row.media)
422	        }
423	        return (deleted, failed)
424	    }

426	    // MARK: - One media's round trip
427	
428	    /// Extract, upload, submit, poll, write, delete — §5a step 3 in that
429	    /// order, and the order is the whole of this method's argument.
430	    ///
431	    /// **The ten-hour refusal is first**, off the media's own `duration`,
432	    /// before a single frame is extracted: an hour of FLAC is about 55 MB and
433	    /// ten hours is 550, and finding out after sending them that AssemblyAI
434	    /// will not take the file is the most expensive possible way to learn it.
435	    ///
436	    /// **The temporary audio is removed in a `defer`**, which covers every
437	    /// exit this method has — the throw from `upload`, the throw from
438	    /// `submit`, the poll that timed out, the cancel — because an extract is
439	    /// an input to one upload and a run that failed must leave nothing in
440	    /// `NSTemporaryDirectory()` behind it. `cloud_captions_probe.py`'s row T
441	    /// globs for `framejob-upload-*` during and after a failed run rather than
442	    /// taking this comment's word for it.
443	    ///
444	    /// **The cache file is written BEFORE its marker, and the marker only
445	    /// when the file LANDED.** Either order can be interrupted; this one
446	    /// fails safe. A file with no marker is re-fetched next run (`isCurrent`
447	    /// needs both); a marker with no file would certify a transcript that is
448	    /// not there, and a marker over an OLDER file — which is what discarding
449	    /// `write`'s answer produced — certifies one that is there and is not the
450	    /// one that was asked for (the reader review, §10.13 R1·3).
451	    ///
452	    /// **The DELETE is last and its answer is recorded**, not assumed
453	    /// (R6-4). `poll` already deletes on every throwing exit of its own, so
454	    /// the only transcript this method can leave behind is one it fetched
455	    /// successfully and then failed to delete — which is what the janitor
456	    /// above is for, and what `remote_deleted: false` in the file means.
457	    func fetch(
458	        media: MediaSnapshot, url: URL, stamp: TranscriptStamp, options: TranscriptOptions,
459	        cancel: Transcriber.CancelToken,
460	        progress: @escaping (CloudProgress.Phase, Double, String) -> Void
461	    ) throws -> (file: MediaTranscript.File, uploaded: Report.Uploaded) {
462	        guard let client else { throw AccessError.credentialRequired }
463	        let name = media.name
464	        let seconds = ReelTime.seconds(media.duration)
465	        guard seconds <= Double(AssemblyAIClient.maxMediaSeconds) else {
466	            throw MediaError.tooLong(name)
467	        }
468	
469	        // 16 kHz mono is what `Transcriber+Extract.swift` writes, so the
470	        // frames a whole track will produce are its seconds times the rate —
471	        // the denominator the extract's progress is measured against.
472	        let expected = max(1, seconds * 16000)
473	        progress(.extracting, 0, CloudProgress.detail(.extracting, file: name))
474	        let upload = try Transcriber.extractUpload(
475	            url: url, name: name, cancel: cancel,
476	            progress: { frames in
477	                progress(
478	                    .extracting, Double(frames) / expected,
479	                    CloudProgress.detail(.extracting, file: name))
480	            })
481	        defer { try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: upload.url) }
482	
483	        let bytes = Int64(
484	            (try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: upload.url.path))?[.size]
485	                .flatMap { ($0 as? NSNumber)?.int64Value } ?? 0)
486	        progress(.uploading, 0, CloudProgress.detail(.uploading, file: name, sent: 0, total: bytes))
487	        let audioURL = try client.upload(
488	            file: upload.url, cancel: cancel,
489	            progress: { sent, total in
490	                let whole = total > 0 ? total : bytes
491	                progress(
492	                    .uploading, whole > 0 ? Double(sent) / Double(whole) : 0,
493	                    CloudProgress.detail(.uploading, file: name, sent: sent, total: whole))
494	            })
495	
496	        progress(.submitting, 0, CloudProgress.detail(.submitting, file: name))
497	        let id = try client.submit(TranscriptRequest(audioURL: audioURL, options: options))
498	        progress(.waiting, 0, CloudProgress.detail(.waiting, file: name, waited: 0))
499	        let fetched = try client.poll(
500	            id: id, audioSeconds: upload.seconds, cancel: cancel,
501	            waited: { waited in
502	                progress(
503	                    .waiting, CloudProgress.waiting(waited: waited, audioSeconds: upload.seconds),
504	                    CloudProgress.detail(.waiting, file: name, waited: waited))
505	            })
506	
507	        progress(.saving, 0, CloudProgress.detail(.saving, file: name))
508	        // The SERVER's two strings, filtered once: each goes into the cache
509	        // header, the report, the MCP `note` and the report card, and a
510	        // server that echoes the key would put it in all four (#187, R2·1).
511	        // Then bounded, and in that order, so a cut never splits the key
512	        // into a piece the filter no longer recognises (#200).
513	        let model = fetched.response.speechModelUsed.map(client.withoutCredential).map(Self.bounded)
514	        let language = fetched.response.languageCode.map(client.withoutCredential).map(Self.bounded)

516	            provider: MediaTranscript.provider, transcriptID: fetched.response.id,
517	            requested: options, speechModelUsed: model,
518	            languageCode: language,
519	            languageConfidence: fetched.response.languageConfidence,
520	            // Floored at 0: a negative duration is no bill (#187, item 3).
521	            audioDuration: max(
522	                0, fetched.response.audioDuration ?? Int(upload.seconds.rounded(.up))),
523	            extractedSeconds: upload.seconds, uploadedFormat: upload.format.rawValue,
524	            // ALWAYS 0 — C0's q4 measured that an extract keeps a late audio
525	            // track's head, so a word's millisecond in the extract is its
526	            // millisecond in the media (`MediaTranscript.Header`'s own doc).
527	            audioTrackStartMs: 0, fetchedAt: Self.timestamp(), remoteDeleted: false)
528	        var file = try MediaTranscript.File(header: header, wordsJSON: fetched.wordsJSON)
529	        // R6-3 keeps the served words VERBATIM, so words that repeat the key
530	        // cannot be rewritten: they are refused, and the transcript deleted,
531	        // before a byte is written (#187, R2·1). Every string literal of the
532	        // served bytes is read too, decoded — every key and value at any
533	        // depth, every value of a repeated key, read or not by
534	        // `TranscriptWord` — because an escaped key is not the key's bytes
535	        // (#200, R6-23). `wordsBytes` already decoded these words, so a
536	        // scan that fails is a fail-safe refusal, not an expected path.
537	        guard let served = TranscriptWord.servedStrings(in: fetched.wordsJSON) else {
538	            throw client.refusing(
539	                .malformed("the transcript's words did not decode"), id: fetched.response.id,
540	                cancel: cancel)
541	        }
542	        if client.carriesCredential(String(decoding: fetched.wordsJSON, as: UTF8.self))
543	            || served.contains(where: client.carriesCredential)
544	        {
545	            throw client.refusing(
546	                .malformed("the transcript's words repeat the API key"), id: fetched.response.id,
547	                cancel: cancel)
548	        }
549	        // ONLY when the file really landed. `write` answers `false` for every
550	        // way it can fail, and discarding that answer stamped the marker over
551	        // a cache file that still held an EARLIER request's words: `isCurrent`
552	        // then read the new marker and the old file and served the stale
553	        // transcript for ever, for a request it was never made from (the
554	        // reader review, §10.13 R1·3). The comment above says the marker
555	        // comes second so it fails safe; this is what makes that true.
556	        let transcriptWritten = MediaTranscript.write(file, for: media.id, in: cacheDirectory)
557	        // Its answer is KEPT: a marker that did not land means this
558	        // transcript was not kept for reuse, and the caller says so (#187,
559	        // item 2).
560	        let stampWritten = transcriptWritten
561	            && MediaTranscript.writeStamp(stamp, for: media.id, in: cacheDirectory)
562	
563	        let deleted = client.delete(id: fetched.response.id, cancel: cancel) == .deleted
564	        // Only over a first write that LANDED. A rewrite after a failed one
565	        // replaces whatever file was there — perhaps the one record of an
566	        // older id still owed a delete — and records this delete in a file
567	        // this request never wrote (#187, item 1; R6-15).
568	        if deleted && transcriptWritten {
569	            file.header.remoteDeleted = true
570	            MediaTranscript.write(file, for: media.id, in: cacheDirectory)
571	        }
572	        return (
573	            file,
574	            Report.Uploaded(
575	                media: media.id, speechModelUsed: model,
576	                languageCode: language,
577	                languageConfidence: fetched.response.languageConfidence,
578	                audioSeconds: header.audioDuration, format: upload.format,
579	                transcriptWritten: transcriptWritten,
580	                stampWritten: stampWritten,
581	                remoteDeleted: deleted)
582	        )
583	    }
584	
585	    /// The most Unicode scalars a string the SERVER names — the model and
586	    /// the language — may keep in the report, the cache header, the MCP
587	    /// answer and the report card (#200).
588	    static let serverStringLimit = 64
589	
590	    /// At most `serverStringLimit` Unicode scalars: a longer string is its
591	    /// first 63 scalars + "…" (U+2026), cut by the one scalar cutter. Not in
592	    /// `withoutCredential`, because the relayed 4xx and `error` sentences
593	    /// take their own, longer limit (`AssemblyAIClient.relayed`, R6-23).
594	    static func bounded(_ text: String) -> String {
595	        AssemblyAIClient.bounded(text, limit: serverStringLimit)
596	    }
597	
598	    /// `fetched_at`, ISO-8601 in UTC — the one spelling of a time in the
599	    /// cache file, and a fixed one: a local-time stamp would make two
600	    /// machines' files differ over nothing.
601	    private static func timestamp() -> String {
602	        let formatter = ISO8601DateFormatter()
603	        formatter.formatOptions = [.withInternetDateTime]
604	        formatter.timeZone = TimeZone(secondsFromGMT: 0)
605	        return formatter.string(from: Date())
606	    }
607	}

610	/// The cloud run result and its shared cleanup wording.
611	extension CloudTranscriber {
612	
613	    /// Everything a caller may want to SAY about a run that the `Outcome`
614	    /// has no room for — which media were uploaded and what AssemblyAI said
615	    /// about each, which were served from the cache, and what the janitor
616	    /// managed.
617	    ///
618	    /// It is beside the outcome rather than inside it because `Outcome` is
619	    /// the shape BOTH engines answer and the on-device one has nothing to
620	    /// put in any of these fields. The tool reads it for its result keys and
621	    /// c1-chrome's report card reads it for its lines.
622	    struct Report: Equatable {
623	
624	        /// One media this run sent to AssemblyAI, and what came back.
625	        struct Uploaded: Equatable {
626	            let media: UInt32
627	            /// R6-8: which model actually ran, so a fallback is reported.
628	            let speechModelUsed: String?
629	            let languageCode: String?
630	            /// Set when the language was DETECTED, not when it was named.
631	            let languageConfidence: Double?
632	            /// Seconds as AssemblyAI reported them — what was billed.
633	            let audioSeconds: Int
634	            let format: Transcriber.UploadFormat
635	            /// Whether this fetched transcript's initial JSON write landed.
636	            let transcriptWritten: Bool
637	            /// Whether the marker landed. Always false when
638	            /// `transcriptWritten` is: the marker only follows its file.
639	            let stampWritten: Bool
640	            /// Whether the remote transcript is confirmed gone (R6-4).
641	            let remoteDeleted: Bool
642	        }
643	
644	        var uploaded: [Uploaded] = []
645	        /// Media served from `cache/transcripts/` with no request at all.
646	        var cached: [UInt32] = []
647	        /// Media whose earlier transcript the janitor deleted this run.
648	        var janitorDeleted: [UInt32] = []
649	        /// Media whose earlier transcript the janitor could NOT delete.
650	        var janitorFailed: [UInt32] = []
651	        /// Pending remote deletes retained because a keyless run sent no requests.
652	        var janitorDeferred: [UInt32] = []
653	        /// R6-11: in `janitorFailed` AND this run would otherwise have
654	        /// fetched them. A held media is in neither `uploaded` nor `cached`
655	        /// and its clips are reported as problems: its cache file is the one
656	        /// record of an id we still have to delete, and a fetch would
657	        /// overwrite it.
658	        var held: [UInt32] = []
659	        /// Media whose transcript was refused after AssemblyAI made it and
660	        /// whose DELETE answered `failed`. No file holds its id, so it is
661	        /// owed with no retry (R6-20).
662	        var refusedUndeleted: [UInt32] = []
663	
664	        /// What was billed: every uploaded media's `audioSeconds`, the one
665	        /// reducer `AgentServer`'s bill sentence and its `audio_seconds` key
666	        /// both read.
667	        ///
668	        /// SATURATING, because every term is the SERVER's own
669	        /// `audio_duration` and `+` traps: two media answered
670	        /// `9223372036854775807` killed the whole app after both had been
671	        /// uploaded and billed (the reader review, §10.13 R1·1). Each term is
672	        /// floored at 0 first, so the sum only grows and an overflow can only
673	        /// be upward: `Int.max` is sticky, and a later negative term cannot
674	        /// pull a saturated total back down (#187, item 4).
675	        var billedSeconds: Int {
676	            uploaded.reduce(0) { sum, row in
677	                let (total, overflowed) = sum.addingReportingOverflow(max(0, row.audioSeconds))
678	                return overflowed ? Int.max : total
679	            }
680	        }
681	
682	        /// One sentence per uploaded media whose marker did not land, in
683	        /// `uploaded` order (#187, item 2).
684	        ///
685	        /// It states only what `fetch` knows and promises nothing about the
686	        /// next run: on a `refresh` run over a current cache an older file
687	        /// and marker equal to this stamp survive the failed write and are
688	        /// served next time — the rule `AgentServer.billed`'s doc records
689	        /// (issue #29).
690	        func cacheWarnings(name: (UInt32) -> String) -> [String] {
691	            uploaded.filter { !$0.stampWritten }.map {
692	                "The transcript of \(name($0.media)) could not be kept in the project for reuse."
693	            }
694	        }
695	
696	        /// Cleanup still owed, in stable per-media order. An ID can be
697	        /// retried only when its transcript JSON was saved in the project.
698	        func deletionWarnings(name: (UInt32) -> String) -> [String] {
699	            var seen: Set<UInt32> = []
700	            var warnings: [String] = []
701	            func append(_ id: UInt32, written: Bool) {
702	                guard seen.insert(id).inserted else { return }
703	                let target = name(id)
704	                var warning: String
705	                if written {
706	                    warning = "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of \(target); "
707	                        + "it will be retried at the next run with an API key."
708	                } else {
709	                    warning = "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of \(target). "
710	                        + "Its transcript could not be saved in the project, so Frame Job cannot "
711	                        + "retry deleting it automatically. Delete it in your AssemblyAI dashboard."
712	                }
713	                if held.contains(id) { warning += " It was not uploaded again in this run." }
714	                warnings.append(warning)
715	            }
716	            for id in janitorFailed { append(id, written: true) }
717	            for id in janitorDeferred where seen.insert(id).inserted {
718	                warnings.append(
719	                    "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of \(name(id)); "
720	                        + "cleanup was deferred because no API key is set. Its deletion ID is "
721	                        + "retained in the project; a later run with a key for the originating "
722	                        + "account and region will retry deletion only if that ID is safe to send.")
723	            }
724	            for row in uploaded where !row.remoteDeleted {
725	                append(row.media, written: row.transcriptWritten)
726	            }
727	            for id in refusedUndeleted { append(id, written: false) }
728	            return warnings
729	        }
730	    }

737	/// The run's one exit and the menu command that opens the sheet: `finish`,
738	/// the single place all four outcomes land (`summary` is the sentence it
739	/// writes), `viewDidDisappear`, which cancels a
740	/// run the sheet is dismissed out from under, and File ▸ Generate
741	/// Captions… itself with the validator arm that greys it.
742	///
743	/// A pure move out of `TranscribeSheetController.swift`, road map 6's C1
744	/// toll 3. Both blocks came here whole and in their own order, with every
745	/// line byte-identical. One widening in the move — `finish` is internal
746	/// rather than `private`, which the compiler forces, since `begin` stayed
747	/// behind and calls it — and nine in the file it left, the stored
748	/// properties `finish` and `viewDidDisappear` read. `summary` stays
749	/// `private`: only `finish` calls it, and it moved with it. W2 deleted
750	/// `truncationText` with the ceiling it reported (spec §11 W-8).
751	///
752	/// **c1-chrome added the cloud engine's three lines** (road map 6 §5e), and
753	/// it is no longer only a move. `cloudReportLines` turns the run's `Report`
754	/// into what the card says beside today's counts — R6-8's fallback, the
755	/// language that was DETECTED and how sure the service was, and any media
756	/// whose remote delete is still owed. They are added in BOTH arms: a run
757	/// that failed can still have uploaded one media and owe a delete for it,
758	/// and a card that printed only the error would lose the one record a
759	/// person has of that.
760	extension TranscribeSheetController {
761	
762	    // MARK: - Commit
763	
764	    /// The one exit for all four outcomes — finished, finished with something
765	    /// to say, failed and cancelled.
766	    ///
767	    /// The plan is built HERE, against the document's CURRENT handle, not
768	    /// against the snapshot this sheet opened with: recognition is minutes
769	    /// long and an agent can edit a document while a sheet is up, and
770	    /// `CaptionLayout.place` reads ids off a probe of the handle it is given.
771	    /// The commit goes through `performGroupedEdit` because a queue completion
772	    /// is not an AppKit event — the road map says `applyEdit` here, and
773	    /// following it would silently merge the captions into whatever edit came
774	    /// before them (app/CLAUDE.md's undo pitfall).
775	    func finish(_ outcome: Result<Transcriber.Outcome, any Error>) {
776	        guard !didFinish else { return }
777	        didFinish = true
778	        bar.doubleValue = 1
779	        stopButton.title = "Close"
780	        stopButton.isEnabled = true
781	        detailLabel.stringValue = ""
782	
783	        let cloudLines = cloudReport.map {
784	            Self.cloudReportLines($0, names: mediaNames, detected: cloudDetected)
785	        } ?? []
786	        let result: Transcriber.Outcome
787	        switch outcome {
788	        case .failure(let error):
789	            statusLabel.stringValue = ([error.localizedDescription] + cloudLines)
790	                .joined(separator: "\n")
791	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
792	            return
793	        case .success(let value):
794	            result = value
795	        }
796	        guard let document = document else {
797	            statusLabel.stringValue = "The project closed before the captions could be placed."
798	            return
799	        }
800	        let plan: CaptionLayout.Plan
801	        do {
802	            let replacing = replaceExisting
803	                ? CaptionLayout.replaceableTracks(
804	                    in: document.editedProject.snapshot, jobs: jobs(in: scope))
805	                : []
806	            plan = try CaptionLayout.place(
807	                result.cues, problems: result.problems, in: document.editedProject,
808	                style: style, looks: looks, replacing: replacing)
809	        } catch {
810	            statusLabel.stringValue = error.localizedDescription
811	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
812	            return
813	        }
814	        document.performGroupedEdit("Generate Captions", plan.ops)
815	
816	        // A clean run has nothing to say that the timeline does not already
817	        // show, so it leaves rather than making the user dismiss a receipt.
818	        guard plan.report.isEmpty, cloudLines.isEmpty else {
819	            statusLabel.stringValue =
820	                ([summary(plan), plan.report] + cloudLines)
821	                .filter { !$0.isEmpty }.joined(separator: "\n")
822	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
823	            return
824	        }
825	        dismiss(self)
826	    }
827	
828	    /// The media names this sheet opened with, by id — the report card names
829	    /// FILES, because a person chose files and an id is the tool's
830	    /// vocabulary.
831	    private var mediaNames: [UInt32: String] {
832	        var out: [UInt32: String] = [:]
833	        for entry in snapshot.media { out[entry.id] = entry.name }
834	        return out
835	    }
836	
837	    /// The cloud run's extra lines, in a fixed order: R6-8's fallback, the
838	    /// detected language, what is still owed a delete, then any fetched
839	    /// transcript that could not be kept for reuse.
840	    ///
841	    /// The owed list is `Report.deletionWarnings`'s rule: once per media
842	    /// id, because a media can be in `janitorFailed` (an id owed from an
843	    /// earlier run) AND in `uploaded` with `remoteDeleted` false (one owed
844	    /// from this run), and saying it twice would read as two transcripts. A
845	    /// media R6-11 HELD gets one more clause, because "it will be retried"
846	    /// is only half of what happened to it.
847	    static func cloudReportLines(
848	        _ report: CloudTranscriber.Report, names: [UInt32: String], detected: Bool
849	    ) -> [String] {
850	        func name(_ id: UInt32) -> String { names[id] ?? "media \(id)" }
851	        var lines: [String] = []
852	        let preferred = TranscriptOptions.shippedModels.first ?? "universal-3-5-pro"
853	        for row in report.uploaded {
854	            guard let model = row.speechModelUsed, model != preferred else { continue }
855	            lines.append(
856	                "“\(name(row.media))” was transcribed with \(model), not \(preferred).")
857	        }
858	        if detected {
859	            for row in report.uploaded {
860	                guard let code = row.languageCode else { continue }
861	                let spoken = AssemblyAILanguages.entry(code: code)?.displayName ?? code
862	                guard let confidence = row.languageConfidence else {
863	                    lines.append("“\(name(row.media))”: detected \(spoken).")
864	                    continue
865	                }
866	                let percent = Int((min(max(confidence, 0), 1) * 100).rounded())
867	                lines.append(
868	                    "“\(name(row.media))”: detected \(spoken) (\(percent)% confidence).")
869	            }
870	        }
871	        lines.append(contentsOf: report.deletionWarnings { "“\(name($0))”" })
872	        lines.append(contentsOf: report.cacheWarnings { "“\(name($0))”" })
873	        return lines
874	    }
875	
876	    private func summary(_ plan: CaptionLayout.Plan) -> String {
877	        "\(plan.clips) caption\(plan.clips == 1 ? "" : "s") added"
878	            + (plan.trackName.map { " on “\($0)”." } ?? ".")
879	    }
880	
881	    override func viewDidDisappear() {
882	        super.viewDidDisappear()
883	        // A sheet that goes away mid-run must not leave a recognition holding
884	        // a temporary file and somebody's compute.
885	        if didStart, !didFinish { token.cancel() }
886	    }
887	}

4	/// piece of chrome for something PERSISTED beyond view state.
5	///
6	/// **A window and not a sheet, deliberately.** A sheet belongs to a document
7	/// and these settings belong to the person: the key and the region are the
8	/// same whichever project is open, and the Settings item has to work with no
9	/// document open at all (`WelcomeWindowController` is what is on screen
10	/// then). `ExportQueueWindowController` is the mould — one instance for the
11	/// life of the process, `isReleasedWhenClosed = false` because the controller
12	/// owns the window, `applyBackground()` in `show()` so a window reopened
13	/// after an appearance change repaints, and no frame autosave, because this
14	/// window is one fixed lockup and remembering where it was is not worth a
15	/// key. It is NOT `isExcludedFromWindowsMenu`: unlike the queue, nothing in
16	/// the Window menu opens it, so AppKit's own row is the only way back to a
17	/// window the person has buried.
18	///
19	/// **Four panes, "MCP", "Assistant", "Transcription" then "Playback"** (issue
20	/// batch B74's `MCPSettingsPane`, spec §11 MC-7; road map 12 A2's
21	/// `AssistantSettingsPane`; `transcriptionPane`; then G-38's
22	/// `PlaybackSettingsPane`), each a vertical stack
23	/// and each one of `content`'s arranged subviews, 24 pt apart through
24	/// `content.spacing`. §5d's one pane was taken as a HEADING inside a window
25	/// titled Settings rather than as a tab bar with one tab. The Assistant,
26	/// Transcription and Playback panes open with `settingsSectionHeader` — a heading and a
27	/// `SettingsInfoButton` whose popover holds its explanation (spec §11 SH-5);
28	/// the MCP pane opens with its bare heading and shows its blurb, because
29	/// MC-7 asked for the text above its button. There is still a Transcription
30	/// section, so the sentence the `transcribe` tool and its catalog entry both
31	/// print — the one that sends a caller to Settings and then to Transcription
32	/// — stays true without either of them being edited. The window's first
33	/// responder is the Assistant key field, so the MCP pane's selectable path

277	        guard let window, let visible, let cap = heightCap else { return }

280	        window.layoutIfNeeded()

282	        frame.origin.y = min(max(frame.minY, visible.minY), visible.maxY - frame.height)
283	        if frame != window.frame { window.setFrame(frame, display: false) }
284	    }

467	/// ran against, the transcriber it holds while it runs, and whether its

469	/// `SettingsWindowController.swift` (#58); the stored `verifying` stays there,

472	    struct VerificationInput: Equatable {
473	        let credential: String
474	        let region: AssemblyAIConfiguration.Region
475	        let base: URL
476	    }

478	    struct Verification {
479	        let id: UUID
480	        let input: VerificationInput
481	        let transcriber: CloudTranscriber
482	    }

484	    func effectiveCredential(storedCredential: String?) -> String? {
485	        let typed = keyField.stringValue.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
486	        if !typed.isEmpty { return typed }
487	        if let storedCredential { return storedCredential }
488	        guard let value = environment[AssemblyAIConfiguration.environmentKey] else { return nil }
489	        let trimmed = value.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
490	        return trimmed.isEmpty ? nil : trimmed
491	    }

493	    func verificationInput(credential: String) throws -> VerificationInput {
494	        VerificationInput(
495	            credential: credential,
496	            region: AssemblyAIConfiguration.region(defaults: defaults),
497	            base: try AssemblyAIConfiguration.baseURL(defaults: defaults))
498	    }

500	    func updateVerifyButton(credential: String?) {
501	        guard let credential else {
502	            verifyButton?.isEnabled = false
503	            return
504	        }
505	        if let verifying,
506	            (try? verificationInput(credential: credential)) == verifying.input
507	        {
508	            verifyButton?.isEnabled = false
509	        } else {
510	            verifyButton?.isEnabled = true
511	        }
512	    }

514	    /// The cheapest authenticated call there is, against whatever key would
515	    /// be used for a real run: what is in the FIELD when somebody has typed
516	    /// one and not saved it yet, and the resolved credential otherwise.
517	    @objc func verifyClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
518	        verifying = nil
519	        guard let credential = effectiveCredential(storedCredential: store().read()) else {
520	            updateVerifyButton(credential: nil)
521	            say("No API key is set.", problem: false)
522	            return
523	        }
524	        let input: VerificationInput
525	        do {
526	            input = try verificationInput(credential: credential)
527	        } catch {
528	            updateVerifyButton(credential: credential)
529	            say(error.localizedDescription, problem: true)
530	            return
531	        }
532	        say("Checking…", problem: false)
533	        verifyButton.isEnabled = false
534	        // The cache directory and the media list are what a RUN needs and a
535	        // verify never touches; the temporary folder is the honest "nowhere".
536	        let transcriber = CloudTranscriber(
537	            client: AssemblyAIClient(base: input.base, credential: input.credential),
538	            cacheDirectory: URL(fileURLWithPath: NSTemporaryDirectory(), isDirectory: true),
539	            media: [:])
540	        let id = UUID()
541	        verifying = Verification(id: id, input: input, transcriber: transcriber)
542	        transcriber.verify { [weak self] answer in
543	            self?.completeVerification(answer, id: id, input: input)
544	        }
545	    }
546	
547	    private func completeVerification(
548	        _ answer: Result<Void, AssemblyAIClient.ClientError>,
549	        id: UUID, input: VerificationInput
550	    ) {
551	        guard verifying?.id == id else { return }
552	        verifying = nil
553	        let credential = effectiveCredential(storedCredential: store().read())
554	        updateVerifyButton(credential: credential)
555	        guard let credential,
556	            (try? verificationInput(credential: credential)) == input
557	        else {
558	            say("Settings changed since this check began. Verify again.", problem: false)
559	            return
560	        }
561	        switch answer {
562	        case .success:
563	            say("Key accepted", problem: false)
564	        case .failure(let error):
565	            say(error.localizedDescription, problem: true)
566	        }
567	    }

571	/// The two things that make an AssemblyAI client, resolved in one place: WHERE
572	/// it speaks (the base URL) and WHAT it says it is (the credential). R6-6 —
573	/// the protocol boundary is exactly this pair, so the stand-in server of road
574	/// map 6 §5i, the EU endpoint and a same-protocol relay are configurations
575	/// and not code.
576	///
577	/// **R6-9, the rule this file is the whole of.** A proof-launched app must
578	/// never open the person's stored key. `-RCSecretFolder <path>` overrides the
579	/// store's folder; with `-RCAssemblyAIEndpoint` set and no `-RCSecretFolder`,
580	/// NO `FileStore` is built at all and `store()` answers an empty
581	/// `MemoryStore`, so an app pointed at a stand-in has the environment as its
582	/// only credential. Both arguments are read ONLY out of the ARGUMENT domain,
583	/// so a persisted default — `UserDefaults`, a plist somebody wrote, a
584	/// leftover from another session — can redirect neither. Without that rule a
585	/// machine where the person had saved a real key would send it to a server
586	/// that writes every header to disk.
587	///
588	/// **`AppSupport.directory` is touched in exactly one line of this file** and
589	/// nowhere else in the feature, which is what makes "no proof reads the real
590	/// folder" checkable by reading rather than by hoping.
591	enum AssemblyAIConfiguration {
592	
593	    /// The endpoint override, the `-RCRecordingFolder` idiom
594	    /// (`RecordingSetup.swift`). A whole base URL rather than a host, because
595	    /// the scheme is part of what is being overridden: the stand-in speaks
596	    /// plain HTTP.
597	    static let endpointArgument = "RCAssemblyAIEndpoint"
598	
599	    /// The store-folder override (R6-9). A PATH, never a key — `ps` shows
600	    /// every launch argument to every user on the machine, which is the same
601	    /// reason R6-5 keeps the credential out of `transcribe`'s arguments.
602	    static let secretFolderArgument = "RCSecretFolder"
603	
604	    /// The persisted region, the Settings window's popup.
605	    static let regionKey = "FrameJobAssemblyAIRegion"
606	
607	    /// The environment override, read only when the store has nothing
608	    /// (R6-5, R6-9 (d)).
609	    static let environmentKey = "RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY"
610	
611	    /// AssemblyAI's two data regions (road map 6 §2). A transcript made in
612	    /// one is not visible in the other, which is why this is a setting and
613	    /// not a fallback.
614	    enum Region: String, CaseIterable {
615	        case us
616	        case eu
617	
618	        var base: URL {
619	            switch self {
620	            case .us: return Region.url("https://api.assemblyai.com")
621	            case .eu: return Region.url("https://api.eu.assemblyai.com")
622	            }
623	        }
624	
625	        /// `URL(string:)` is optional because its input is usually somebody
626	        /// else's; these two are literals on the lines above. A parse that
627	        /// failed would be a typo there, and the fallback reaches no host at
628	        /// all — every request against it refuses, which is the safe
629	        /// direction: never a DIFFERENT server.
630	        private static func url(_ text: String) -> URL {
631	            URL(string: text) ?? URL(fileURLWithPath: "/dev/null")
632	        }
633	
634	        var displayName: String {
635	            switch self {
636	            case .us: return "United States"
637	            case .eu: return "European Union"
638	            }
639	        }
640	    }
641	
642	    /// Why a configured endpoint cannot be used, in a sentence the Settings
643	    /// window and a tool can both print.
644	    enum ConfigurationError: LocalizedError, Equatable {
645	        case malformedEndpoint(String)
646	        case insecureEndpoint(String)
647	
648	        var errorDescription: String? {
649	            switch self {
650	            case .malformedEndpoint(let text):
651	                return "“\(text)” is not a URL the transcription service can be reached at."
652	            case .insecureEndpoint(let host):
653	                return "A plain HTTP endpoint is only allowed for a local server, and "
654	                    + "“\(host)” is not one."
655	            }
656	        }
657	    }
658	
659	    /// The region the person chose. An unknown or absent value is `.us`, not
660	    /// an error: a defaults file written by a later build, or by hand, must
661	    /// not stop the app from transcribing.
662	    static func region(defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) -> Region {
663	        guard let raw = defaults.string(forKey: regionKey), let region = Region(rawValue: raw)
664	        else { return .us }
665	        return region
666	    }
667	
668	    /// Where the client speaks: the argument-domain endpoint when one is set,
669	    /// the region's own host otherwise.
670	    static func baseURL(defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) throws -> URL {
671	        guard let override = argument(endpointArgument, defaults: defaults) else {
672	            return region(defaults: defaults).base
673	        }
674	        guard let url = URL(string: override), let scheme = url.scheme?.lowercased(),
675	            let host = url.host, !host.isEmpty
676	        else { throw ConfigurationError.malformedEndpoint(override) }
677	        guard scheme == "http" || scheme == "https" else {
678	            throw ConfigurationError.malformedEndpoint(override)
679	        }
680	        // Plain HTTP for a loopback host only. C0's q3 measured that macOS
681	        // 26.5.1 does not block it from an ad-hoc-signed hardened-runtime
682	        // bundle with no ATS key at all, which is why `project.yml` carries
683	        // none — and this guard is what keeps that measurement from becoming
684	        // a licence to send a key over the open network in clear.
685	        guard scheme == "https" || isLoopback(host) else {
686	            throw ConfigurationError.insecureEndpoint(host)
687	        }
688	        return url
689	    }
690	
691	    /// The `SecretStore` this process may use, and R6-9's whole decision in
692	    /// one function.
693	    ///
694	    /// With `-RCSecretFolder` set, a `FileStore` on that folder: a proof's
695	    /// own disposable directory. With no `-RCSecretFolder` but
696	    /// `-RCAssemblyAIEndpoint` set, an EMPTY `MemoryStore`: the app has been
697	    /// pointed at something that is not AssemblyAI, so the person's stored
698	    /// key is not opened at all and `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` is the only
699	    /// credential such a run can have. With neither, the person's own file

title: AI features and your own keys
description: Which features need nothing, which use an on-device model, which need your own Anthropic or AssemblyAI key, and what ever leaves your Mac.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Most of Frame Job needs no key and no network. The few features that send your words or audio to a cloud model run on your own API keys, so you decide what's used and you pay the provider directly.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
  keys="⌘,"
  where={['Settings ▸ Assistant', 'Settings ▸ Transcription']}
  tools={['transcribe', 'transcribe_for_fillers']}
  needs="Your own Anthropic or AssemblyAI key, only for the features that send to them."
/>

## Your own keys

There's no Frame Job account and no relay in between. There are two keys in all, and each provider bills your account directly.

| Key | Turns on | Saved in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anthropic | The Assistant | [Settings ▸ Assistant](/assistant/set-up/) |
| AssemblyAI | Cloud captions and Remove Filler Words | [Settings ▸ Transcription](/captions/assemblyai-key/) |

Frame Job shows its own estimate of what each Assistant turn and each month costs. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/). The provider's bill is the real figure.

With no key set, Settings says "No API key is set." in its ordinary muted colour. That's a state, not an error.

## What needs what

Anything that sends your words or audio to a language or cloud model needs your own key. Everything that runs on your Mac needs none.

| What it takes | Features |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing | Editing, colour, graphics, recording and export |
| An on-device model, with no key and no upload | **Generate Captions** with **On this Mac**, Remove Silences' voice analysis, Enhance Voice and Voice Isolation, Split at Shot Changes, Remove Background, Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version and Switch by Speaker |
| Your AssemblyAI key | The **AssemblyAI** engine of **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, and **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** with its **Transcribe** buttons |
| Your Anthropic key | The Assistant |

Filler removal works only through AssemblyAI. There's no on-device version.

Without your Anthropic key, **View ▸ Assistant** still opens the tab, which says how to add the key.

Work you've already paid for keeps working with no key:

- **Generate** isn't greyed when every file is already transcribed.
- **Remove Filler Words…** stays on while a file it would work on has a current transcript made with filler words.

An on-device language that isn't installed yet shows a **Download** row in the [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) sheet.

## Greyed commands

A command that needs a key you haven't set is greyed rather than hidden, and it says which key and where to set it.

A greyed menu item's title gains the key's name, as in **Remove Filler Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)**. Rest the pointer on a greyed command or button and it reads:

> No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription.

For the Assistant it's the same sentence with Anthropic and Assistant. The Assistant tab itself reads "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." with an **Open Settings…** button.

An agent's tool stops with the same sentence, at the point it would send. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) for what still works without a key.

## Saving a key takes effect at once

Saving or removing a key updates open sheets and menu items straight away. An open Generate Captions sheet turns **Generate** back on with the sheet still up, and there's nothing to reopen or relaunch.

## What stays on this Mac

Editing, analysis, on-device transcription, recording and export all stay on this Mac. Only these reach the network, and each is something you start or can see:

| Goes to | What | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AssemblyAI | The audio of the files being transcribed | When you press **Generate** or **Transcribe** with that engine. **Verify** in Settings also makes a small request with your key, with no audio. See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/). |
| Anthropic | Your Assistant messages, the project's details and the frames it renders | While you use the Assistant. See [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/). |
| GitHub | A request for LiteLLM's published price table, with no key and no project data | At most once a day, from the Assistant's helper |
| GitHub | A check of the update feed | In the [downloaded copy](/getting-started/updates/) only, when you check or if you allowed automatic checks |
| macOS's own download | An on-device speech model | When you ask for one |

Frame Job has no analytics or telemetry code.

---
title: "Transcribe on this Mac"
description: Turn the speech in your clips into captions with your Mac's own speech engine, with no key, no upload and no length limit, and install the languages you need.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

**On this Mac** recognises speech with the engine built into your Mac. It costs nothing, needs no key, and your audio never leaves the machine.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
  where="Generate Captions sheet ▸ Engine: ▸ On this Mac"
  tools={['transcribe', 'get_transcript']}
  needs="The language's speech model, installed on this Mac. No key, and nothing is uploaded."
/>

## Transcribe on this Mac

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.

2. Set **Engine:** to **On this Mac**. The sheet remembers the engine you chose last.

3. Check **Language:**. If it reads "— not installed", [download the language](#download-a-speech-language) first.

4. Choose **Generate**.

</Steps>

<Shot
  name="15-generate-captions-sheet.sheet"
  alt="The Generate Captions sheet with Language set to English (United States), Engine set to On this Mac, From set to Whole timeline and Style set to Subtitles. The paragraph at the top says the words are recognised on this Mac and nothing is uploaded, and the summary reads 2 clips, 00:00:10.200 of audio."
/>

The sheet says what it's about to do: "The words are recognised ON THIS MAC and land as ordinary text clips on a track of their own, so they show in the preview and burn into an export with no further step. Nothing is uploaded."

Frame Job extracts the part of the media each clip plays, and recognises that. There's no length limit, and macOS shows no permission prompt, because the engine reads an extracted audio file and never touches the microphone.

[Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) covers the rest of the sheet: which clips to caption, the style and the progress card. The other engine is [AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/), which runs in the cloud on your own key.

## Choose a language

**Language:** lists every language this Mac's speech engine supports, by name, so the list differs from Mac to Mac. It opens on your Mac's own language, or the nearest one on the list.

A language whose speech model isn't on this Mac reads "— not installed". **Generate** stays greyed until the chosen language is installed.

If the engine names no language at all, the pop-up reads **No on-device language** and the note under the summary says "This Mac's speech engine named no language with an on-device speech model. Reopen this sheet to ask it again." Setting **Engine:** to **AssemblyAI** still works in that state.

## Download a speech language

Speech models are installed per Mac, not per project, and this sheet is the only place Frame Job installs one.

<Steps>

1. Choose a language marked "— not installed". A **Download** button appears under **Language:**.

2. Choose **Download**.

3. Wait for the row to finish. It shows a bar and "Downloading *language*…".

</Steps>

When the download finishes, the language is installed and selected, and **Generate** comes on.

The bar moves without a figure until the download reports its size. Only then does the row add a percentage, such as "Downloading French… 40%". It never shows a size.

While the download runs:

- **Language:** and **Engine:** are locked, and **Generate** stays greyed.
- **Download** becomes **Cancel**, which is greyed until the download has started reporting. Choosing it stops the download with no message.
- The **Cancel** at the bottom of the sheet closes the sheet and leaves the download running. You lose the bar and the way to stop it.

If the download fails, the note reads "The download did not finish:" and gives the reason. The **Download** button is back, so you can try again.

## Every run recognises the audio again

Nothing is kept between runs for captions made on this Mac. Each run, [restyling](/captions/restyle-captions/) included, recognises the audio from the start. That's free, but it takes the time again.

Two things follow from that:

- The sheet's preview never shows on-device words. It shows the first words of a cached [AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#reuse-a-transcript) transcript if the clip has one, and "This is how it looks" if not.
- The words the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-words/) keeps on this Mac are separate, and captions never use them.

## The pause note

With **On this Mac** chosen and a word style picked, a note under the look boxes reads "On-device words rarely carry a pause; this shows mostly with AssemblyAI." It shows whether or not **Dim in pauses** is ticked.

The on-device engine stretches each word's time across the silence after it, so few pauses are long enough for [Dim in pauses](/captions/word-caption-looks/) to act on. The look still works, but you'll see it rarely.

## With an agent

`transcribe` uses this engine by default, whatever the sheet last chose.

An agent can't install a language. A language tag the engine has never heard of is treated as a misspelling, and a tag it knows with no model on this Mac stops with a sentence telling a person to install it from this sheet. `get_transcript` works to the same rules. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

## Related

- [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/)
- [What can be transcribed](/captions/what-can-be-transcribed/)
- [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/)
- [Looks for word captions](/captions/word-caption-looks/)

---
title: "Transcribe with AssemblyAI"
description: Send the audio of your files to AssemblyAI on your own key for captions with speakers, a vocabulary and language detection, see the price first, and reuse each transcript for free.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

**AssemblyAI** is the cloud engine for captions. It adds speaker labels, a vocabulary of names and jargon, and language detection, and its word timing shows real pauses. You pay AssemblyAI directly on your own key, and each file's transcript is kept so you only pay for it once.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
  where="Generate Captions sheet ▸ Engine: ▸ AssemblyAI"
  tools="transcribe"
  needs="Your own AssemblyAI key, unless every file is already transcribed, and a network connection for anything new."
/>

## Transcribe with AssemblyAI

<Steps>

1. [Save your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/) in Settings, if you haven't.

2. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.

3. Set **Engine:** to **AssemblyAI**. The **Speakers:**, **Vocabulary:** and **Transcribe again:** rows appear.

4. Set **Language:**, and any [options](#split-the-words-by-speaker) you want.

5. Read the [price](#the-price-before-you-press-generate) in the summary line.

6. Choose **Generate**. Nothing is uploaded until you do.

</Steps>

The paragraph at the top of the sheet reads "The audio of these files is uploaded to AssemblyAI (United States), transcribed with Universal-3.5 Pro, and deleted from AssemblyAI once the words have been read back. Nothing is uploaded until Generate is pressed." It names your [region](/captions/assemblyai-key/#region), which is United States or European Union.

Each media file goes up once, and every clip on it takes its words from that one transcript. Frame Job asks for Universal-3.5 Pro and allows Universal-2 as a fallback. This engine doesn't use your Mac's speech models, so it works on a Mac that has none.

[What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/) says exactly what leaves your Mac and how it's deleted. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) covers the rest of the sheet.

## The price before you press Generate

The summary line prices the run at AssemblyAI's published rate, and updates as you change a control:

`2 files to upload · 01:12:30.000 of audio · about $0.25 at AssemblyAI's published rate · 1 file already transcribed`

The rate is $0.21 an hour of audio, plus $0.02 an hour with **Speakers:** on. Those are the figures AssemblyAI published on 2026-09-17. They're built into Frame Job and aren't fetched, so AssemblyAI's own bill is the real figure. Each file is priced at its whole length, because AssemblyAI [bills for the whole file](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#what-is-uploaded-and-billed).

A very short run reads "under $0.01". When every file is already transcribed the line starts "Nothing to upload", as in `Nothing to upload · 2 files already transcribed`.

Two more counts can appear, and neither is in the price:

| The line says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "1 file waiting on an earlier delete" | The file [isn't uploaded](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#a-pending-delete-holds-a-file-back) until AssemblyAI confirms an earlier delete. |
| "1 file could not be read" | Frame Job couldn't read the media file, so it can't be transcribed. With nothing else to do, **Generate** is greyed. |

## Why each file uploads

Rest the pointer on the summary line. You get one line for each file that isn't already transcribed, saying why, and then the rate as a dated sentence.

| The line says | What changed |
| --- | --- |
| "has not been transcribed yet" | This file has no transcript in the project. |
| "has changed since it was transcribed" | The file on disk isn't the one that was transcribed. |
| "was transcribed with a different language" | The named setting differs from the transcript's. It can also name **model**, **speakers** or **vocabulary**, or several of them. |
| "was transcribed for a different request" | Something else about the request differs. |
| "is already transcribed, and Transcribe again was asked for" | You ticked [Transcribe again](#transcribe-again). |
| "could not be read, so it cannot be transcribed" | The media file couldn't be read. |

## Split the words by speaker

Tick **Speakers:** ("split by speaker, coloured in Subtitles") to have AssemblyAI label who says what. It's off by default and adds $0.02 an hour to the price.

A change of speaker then always starts a new cue or page. In the [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) style, each speaker's cues take their own colour.

Speakers are counted separately for each media file. A speaker is a label within one file, so the same person in two files can come back as two different speakers.

## Add names and jargon

Type the words you expect into **Vocabulary:**, separated by commas: product names, people, identifiers. AssemblyAI then spells them your way. The field starts empty, and its placeholder reads "names and jargon, separated by commas".

Blank entries and repeats are dropped, keeping the first spelling. The list stops at 1,000 terms, which is AssemblyAI's limit, and it's cut from the end, so put the terms that matter most first. When the limit cuts your list, the note reads "Vocabulary was capped at 1000 terms (AssemblyAI's limit); N were given."

## Choose a language

**Language:** opens on **Detect automatically**, which leaves the language to AssemblyAI. The [result](#what-the-result-says) then tells you what it found.

You can also name one: English, English (Australia), English (United Kingdom), English (United States), Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Arabic, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, Hebrew, Hindi, Japanese, Chinese, Norwegian, Swedish, Turkish or Vietnamese. That list is what AssemblyAI published on 2026-09-17, so it can fall behind.

## Reuse a transcript

Each media file's transcript is kept in the project package, every word as AssemblyAI sent it. A later run that wants the same transcript uses it, with no upload, no request and no cost.

- **The file:** its size, modified time and duration, and whether it has audio. Change the file, or relink to a different one, and it's transcribed again.
- **The model** Frame Job asks for.
- **The language:** **Detect automatically** and a named language count as different, as do two named languages.
- **Speakers:** on or off.
- **Vocabulary:** the same terms in the same order.

| The card says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "“interview.mov”: detected Spanish (97% confidence)." | With **Detect automatically**, the language AssemblyAI found in each file it just transcribed, and how sure it was. The figure is left out if AssemblyAI gave none. |
| "“interview.mov” was transcribed with universal-2, not universal-3-5-pro." | AssemblyAI used the fallback model. |
| "The transcript of “interview.mov” could not be kept in the project for reuse." | The captions are fine, but a later run may upload and bill this file again. |
| "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of…" | See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#what-the-result-warns-about). |

## When a file fails

One file's failure doesn't end a run. Its clips are listed with the reason, and captions from the other files are still placed. If every file fails, nothing is placed and the card shows why.

Two things end a run early, and neither places anything: choosing **Cancel**, and a key AssemblyAI refuses, because every later upload would fail the same way. Files that had already finished stay in the project, so a later run doesn't pay for them again.

| The reason reads | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| "No network connection" | Frame Job couldn't reach AssemblyAI. |
| "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" | AssemblyAI turned the key down, and the run stops there. Try **Verify** in [Settings](/captions/assemblyai-key/#verify). |
| "AssemblyAI answered 500" | AssemblyAI had a problem of its own. The number varies. |
| "AssemblyAI did not finish the transcript in the time allowed." | Frame Job waits at least 5 minutes for a transcript, and longer for audio over about 4 hours. |
| "“name” is longer than AssemblyAI's 10-hour limit for one file." | Nothing was sent for this file. |
| "AssemblyAI may have created a transcript, but Frame Job could not recover its ID…" | The answer to the request was lost. Check your AssemblyAI dashboard before you try again, because a retry could be billed and the transcript may still be there. |
| AssemblyAI's own sentence | AssemblyAI turned the request down, for a reason such as your account's balance, and Frame Job passes on its words. |

AssemblyAI's words include fillers, and captions leave them out, so a caption reads the same whether or not its transcript has them. The sheet's preview leaves them out too.
