---
title: "What goes to AssemblyAI"
description: What leaves your Mac when you transcribe with AssemblyAI, what you're billed for, how the transcript is deleted afterwards, and what happens when a delete doesn't land.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

When you transcribe with AssemblyAI, the sound of your files leaves your Mac, and only after you press **Generate**. Frame Job then asks AssemblyAI to delete its transcript as soon as it has the words. Captions made [on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/) never leave it.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Generate Captions…', 'Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…']}
  where="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription ▸ ⓘ"
  tools="transcribe"
  needs="Your own AssemblyAI key."
/>

## What is uploaded and billed

| Goes to AssemblyAI | Stays on your Mac |
| --- | --- |
| The whole audio of each media file behind the chosen clips | The video |
| Your **Vocabulary:** terms, and the language and **Speakers:** settings | The project and the rest of its media |

The audio goes up as 16 kHz mono FLAC, about half the size of a WAV with the same samples. If the FLAC can't be written, a WAV goes up instead. Frame Job removes its temporary copy from your Mac when the upload ends, whether or not it worked.

It's the whole file, not only the parts your clips use, and AssemblyAI bills for the whole file. A two-hour recording you use 30 seconds of costs two hours, about $0.42 at the rate [Frame Job shows](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#the-price-before-you-press-generate). A file over 10 hours is turned down before anything is sent.

The audio goes to the [region](/captions/assemblyai-key/#region) set in Settings, and the sheet names that region before you press **Generate**. **Transcribe** in [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) sends audio in the same way.

:::caution
A recording of someone else goes to a third party here. Get their say-so first, or use **On this Mac**.
:::

## The transcript is deleted after reading

Each file's round trip runs in this order: upload, transcribe, read the words back, save them in the project package, then ask AssemblyAI to delete its transcript. You don't have to do anything. Each delete request has 5 seconds to answer.

Frame Job also asks for the delete when a transcript fails, runs out of time or can't be used, and when you choose **Cancel** while AssemblyAI is working.

A copy of the words stays in your [project package](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#reuse-a-transcript). That copy is what makes later runs free.

If AssemblyAI doesn't confirm the delete, [the result says so](#what-the-result-warns-about).

## Unconfirmed deletes are retried

An unconfirmed delete is retried at the start of the next AssemblyAI run in the same project that has a key. Every delete the project is owed is retried then, whichever files the run is about.

The retry uses the key and region set at that later run, so it can only work with a key for the account and region that made the upload. The two regions don't share transcripts. If you've changed either since, set it back for a run.

With no key set when that next run starts, nothing is sent, and the delete waits for a run that has one.

## A pending delete holds a file back

While a delete is pending, Frame Job won't upload that file again, because the kept transcript is its only record of what's still owed. If that file's kept transcript still matches the run, it's used as normal. If the file needs a new upload, or you ticked [Transcribe again](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#transcribe-again), it waits:

- The summary line counts it apart, as "1 file waiting on an earlier delete", and leaves it out of the price.
- Resting the pointer on the summary gives its price: "It is waiting on an earlier delete and will not be uploaded in this run — about $0.42 more if it does."

The hover line says "if it does" because the retry happens first. If the delete goes through at the start of the run, the file uploads in that same run. If it doesn't, the file isn't uploaded, and its clips are listed with the reason "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting its earlier transcript, so it was not uploaded again; the next run with an API key retries the delete".

## What the result warns about

These lines appear on the sheet's result card, with the file's name in place of "name".

| The card says | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of “name”; it will be retried at the next run with an API key." | Nothing. Run AssemblyAI again in this project when you next need it, with the same account and region. |
| "…It was not uploaded again in this run." | Added to the line above when the delete held the file back. |
| "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of “name”; cleanup was deferred because no API key is set. Its deletion ID is retained in the project; a later run with a key for the originating account and region will retry deletion only if that ID is safe to send." | Set the key for that account and region, then run again in this project. |
| "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of “name”. Its transcript could not be saved in the project, so Frame Job cannot retry deleting it automatically. Delete it in your AssemblyAI dashboard." | Frame Job has no record to retry from. Choose [Account Page](/captions/assemblyai-key/#open-your-assemblyai-account) in Settings and delete it there. |

:::caution
In an [untitled project](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#transcribe-an-untitled-project), the record of a pending delete lives in a temporary folder. If you never save the project, that record is lost and Frame Job can't retry. Save the project, or delete the transcript in your AssemblyAI dashboard.
:::

## Related

- [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/)
- [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/)
- [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/)
- [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/)

---
title: "Your AssemblyAI key"
description: Save, check and remove the AssemblyAI key that turns on cloud captions and Remove Filler Words, choose your region, and see where the key is kept.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Your AssemblyAI key turns on cloud transcription, and AssemblyAI bills your account directly. It lives in Settings, so it's the same for every project, and you can set it with no project open. For how keys work across Frame Job, see [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/).

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
  keys="⌘,"
  where="Settings ▸ Transcription"
  needs="An AssemblyAI account."
/>

<Shot
  name="02-settings.window"
  alt="The Settings window. Under the Transcription heading, with its info button, are an AssemblyAI API key field reading Paste your key, a Region pop-up set to United States, the line No API key is set, and the buttons Save, Remove, Verify and Account Page. Remove and Verify are greyed."
/>

## Save your AssemblyAI key

<Steps>

1. Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>) and find **Transcription**.

2. Choose **Account Page** to get a key from your AssemblyAI dashboard.

3. Paste the key into **AssemblyAI API key:**.

4. Choose **Save**, or press <kbd>Return</kbd>.

5. Choose [**Verify**](#check-the-key) to check that it works.

</Steps>

The line under the controls says "Key saved.", and the field empties. From then on the field shows a fixed row of dots, the same length whatever your key is. The key itself never goes back in the field, so it can't be read or copied out of the window.

With no key anywhere, the line reads "No API key is set." in ordinary grey. That's a state, not a problem. **Save** with an empty field beeps and does nothing.

If the key file can't be written, the line reads "The API key could not be saved:" and gives the reason. The field is emptied anyway, so paste the key again once it's fixed.

## Check the key

**Verify** makes AssemblyAI's cheapest signed-in request, with your key and region, to see if the key works. It doesn't transcribe or bill anything.

It checks the key a real run would use: the one typed in the field, even if you haven't saved it, then the saved key, then [the environment's](#use-a-key-from-the-environment). A typed key is only checked, so choose **Save** as well to keep it.

| The line says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Checking…" | The request is on its way. |
| "Key accepted" | AssemblyAI accepted the key in this region. |
| "Settings changed since this check began. Verify again." | You changed the key or the region during the check, so its answer no longer applies. |
| AssemblyAI's message, such as "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" | The check failed, and the message says why. "No network connection" is another. |

**Verify** is greyed when there's no key at all, and while a check of the same key and region is running.

## Choose a region

**Region:** chooses the AssemblyAI data centre your audio goes to: **United States**, the default, or **European Union**. It's saved as soon as you pick it, and an open sheet updates straight away. The Generate Captions and Remove Filler Words sheets name the region before you upload.

A transcript made in one region can't be seen from the other, so pick the region your account uses. [A pending delete](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#unconfirmed-deletes-are-retried) only succeeds in the region it was made in.

Changing the region doesn't upload anything again. Transcripts already kept in a project stay usable.

## Open your AssemblyAI account

**Account Page** opens your AssemblyAI dashboard in your browser, at `https://www.assemblyai.com/dashboard`. That's where you get a key and see what you've spent.

## Remove the key

**Remove** deletes the saved key and says "Key removed." It's greyed unless a key is saved.

If the removal fails, the key stays saved and the line says why.

## Where the key is kept

The key is saved in a file only your account can read, not in the Keychain:

`~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/assemblyai-key`

The file's mode is `0600`, and it sits beside `anthropic-key`, the [Assistant](/assistant/set-up/)'s key. Any program running as you can read it, so treat that file like a password. The key is never passed on the command line.

## Use a key from the environment

If no key is saved, Frame Job also accepts one from the `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` environment variable, which is useful when you launch it from a terminal.

- A saved key always wins over the variable.
- An empty variable counts as no key.
- **Verify** checks the variable's key when nothing is typed or saved.
- **Remove** stays greyed, because nothing is saved.

See [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/).

## What the key turns on

| Feature | Without a key |
| --- | --- |
| The **AssemblyAI** engine of [Generate Captions](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) | **Generate** is greyed, [unless every file is already transcribed](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#generate-with-no-key). |
| [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/), which finds fillers only through AssemblyAI | The menu item reads **Remove Filler Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)**. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) for what works without one. |

Captions made [on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/) need no key.

Saving or removing a key, or changing the region, reaches an open Generate Captions sheet straight away, so **Generate** can come on without reopening it.

## What the info button says

The ⓘ beside the **Transcription** heading explains three things:

- **What leaves your Mac.** The audio of the files you're captioning is uploaded, transcribed, read back and then deleted from AssemblyAI. A delete that didn't land is retried at the start of the next run. Nothing is uploaded until you press **Generate**, and captions made on this Mac never leave it.
- **The rate.** AssemblyAI's published rate as Frame Job last read it: $0.21 an hour of audio, and $0.02 more with **Speakers:** on, read on 2026-09-17.
- **The key.** It's kept in a file only you can read and is never shown again once it's saved.

[What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/) has the full story.

## Only a person sets the key

No agent tool can read or change the key or the region, and an agent can't pass a key of its own. Only you set them, here. An agent's `transcribe` call uses the key you've saved, and with none it stops with the same "No AssemblyAI API key is set." sentence.

## Related

- [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/)
- [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/)
- [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/)
- [Settings](/reference/settings/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>

---
title: "Transcribe on this Mac"
description: Turn the speech in your clips into captions with your Mac's own speech engine, with no key, no upload and no length limit, and install the languages you need.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

**On this Mac** recognises speech with the engine built into your Mac. It costs nothing, needs no key, and your audio never leaves the machine.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
  where="Generate Captions sheet ▸ Engine: ▸ On this Mac"
  tools={['transcribe', 'get_transcript']}
  needs="The language's speech model, installed on this Mac. No key, and nothing is uploaded."
/>

## Transcribe on this Mac

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.

2. Set **Engine:** to **On this Mac**. The sheet remembers the engine you chose last.

3. Check **Language:**. If it reads "— not installed", [download the language](#download-a-speech-language) first.

4. Choose **Generate**.

</Steps>

<Shot
  name="15-generate-captions-sheet.sheet"
  alt="The Generate Captions sheet with Language set to English (United States), Engine set to On this Mac, From set to Whole timeline and Style set to Subtitles. The paragraph at the top says the words are recognised on this Mac and nothing is uploaded, and the summary reads 2 clips, 00:00:10.200 of audio."
/>

The sheet says what it's about to do: "The words are recognised ON THIS MAC and land as ordinary text clips on a track of their own, so they show in the preview and burn into an export with no further step. Nothing is uploaded."

Frame Job extracts the part of the media each clip plays, and recognises that. There's no length limit, and macOS shows no permission prompt, because the engine reads an extracted audio file and never touches the microphone.

[Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) covers the rest of the sheet: which clips to caption, the style and the progress card. The other engine is [AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/), which runs in the cloud on your own key.

## Choose a language

**Language:** lists every language this Mac's speech engine supports, by name, so the list differs from Mac to Mac. It opens on your Mac's own language, or the nearest one on the list.

A language whose speech model isn't on this Mac reads "— not installed". **Generate** stays greyed until the chosen language is installed.

If the engine names no language at all, the pop-up reads **No on-device language** and the note under the summary says "This Mac's speech engine named no language with an on-device speech model. Reopen this sheet to ask it again." Setting **Engine:** to **AssemblyAI** still works in that state.

## Download a speech language

Speech models are installed per Mac, not per project, and this sheet is the only place Frame Job installs one.

<Steps>

1. Choose a language marked "— not installed". A **Download** button appears under **Language:**.

2. Choose **Download**.

3. Wait for the row to finish. It shows a bar and "Downloading *language*…".

</Steps>

When the download finishes, the language is installed and selected, and **Generate** comes on.

The bar moves without a figure until the download reports its size. Only then does the row add a percentage, such as "Downloading French… 40%". It never shows a size.

While the download runs:

- **Language:** and **Engine:** are locked, and **Generate** stays greyed.
- **Download** becomes **Cancel**, which is greyed until the download has started reporting. Choosing it stops the download with no message.
- The **Cancel** at the bottom of the sheet closes the sheet and leaves the download running. You lose the bar and the way to stop it.

If the download fails, the note reads "The download did not finish:" and gives the reason. The **Download** button is back, so you can try again.

## Every run recognises the audio again

Nothing is kept between runs for captions made on this Mac. Each run, [restyling](/captions/restyle-captions/) included, recognises the audio from the start. That's free, but it takes the time again.

Two things follow from that:

- The sheet's preview never shows on-device words. It shows the first words of a cached [AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#reuse-a-transcript) transcript if the clip has one, and "This is how it looks" if not.
- The words the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-words/) keeps on this Mac are separate, and captions never use them.

## The pause note

With **On this Mac** chosen and a word style picked, a note under the look boxes reads "On-device words rarely carry a pause; this shows mostly with AssemblyAI." It shows whether or not **Dim in pauses** is ticked.

The on-device engine stretches each word's time across the silence after it, so few pauses are long enough for [Dim in pauses](/captions/word-caption-looks/) to act on. The look still works, but you'll see it rarely.

## With an agent

`transcribe` uses this engine by default, whatever the sheet last chose.

An agent can't install a language. A language tag the engine has never heard of is treated as a misspelling, and a tag it knows with no model on this Mac stops with a sentence telling a person to install it from this sheet. `get_transcript` works to the same rules. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

## Related

- [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/)
- [What can be transcribed](/captions/what-can-be-transcribed/)
- [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/)
- [Looks for word captions](/captions/word-caption-looks/)

---
title: "Transcribe with AssemblyAI"
description: Send the audio of your files to AssemblyAI on your own key for captions with speakers, a vocabulary and language detection, see the price first, and reuse each transcript for free.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

**AssemblyAI** is the cloud engine for captions. It adds speaker labels, a vocabulary of names and jargon, and language detection, and its word timing shows real pauses. You pay AssemblyAI directly on your own key, and each file's transcript is kept so you only pay for it once.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
  where="Generate Captions sheet ▸ Engine: ▸ AssemblyAI"
  tools="transcribe"
  needs="Your own AssemblyAI key, unless every file is already transcribed, and a network connection for anything new."
/>

## Transcribe with AssemblyAI

<Steps>

1. [Save your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/) in Settings, if you haven't.

2. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.

3. Set **Engine:** to **AssemblyAI**. The **Speakers:**, **Vocabulary:** and **Transcribe again:** rows appear.

4. Set **Language:**, and any [options](#split-the-words-by-speaker) you want.

5. Read the [price](#the-price-before-you-press-generate) in the summary line.

6. Choose **Generate**. Nothing is uploaded until you do.

</Steps>

The paragraph at the top of the sheet reads "The audio of these files is uploaded to AssemblyAI (United States), transcribed with Universal-3.5 Pro, and deleted from AssemblyAI once the words have been read back. Nothing is uploaded until Generate is pressed." It names your [region](/captions/assemblyai-key/#region), which is United States or European Union.

Each media file goes up once, and every clip on it takes its words from that one transcript. Frame Job asks for Universal-3.5 Pro and allows Universal-2 as a fallback. This engine doesn't use your Mac's speech models, so it works on a Mac that has none.

[What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/) says exactly what leaves your Mac and how it's deleted. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) covers the rest of the sheet.

## The price before you press Generate

The summary line prices the run at AssemblyAI's published rate, and updates as you change a control:

`2 files to upload · 01:12:30.000 of audio · about $0.25 at AssemblyAI's published rate · 1 file already transcribed`

The rate is $0.21 an hour of audio, plus $0.02 an hour with **Speakers:** on. Those are the figures AssemblyAI published on 2026-09-17. They're built into Frame Job and aren't fetched, so AssemblyAI's own bill is the real figure. Each file is priced at its whole length, because AssemblyAI [bills for the whole file](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#what-is-uploaded-and-billed).

A very short run reads "under $0.01". When every file is already transcribed the line starts "Nothing to upload", as in `Nothing to upload · 2 files already transcribed`.

Two more counts can appear, and neither is in the price:

| The line says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "1 file waiting on an earlier delete" | The file [isn't uploaded](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#a-pending-delete-holds-a-file-back) until AssemblyAI confirms an earlier delete. |
| "1 file could not be read" | Frame Job couldn't read the media file, so it can't be transcribed. With nothing else to do, **Generate** is greyed. |

## Why each file uploads

Rest the pointer on the summary line. You get one line for each file that isn't already transcribed, saying why, and then the rate as a dated sentence.

| The line says | What changed |
| --- | --- |
| "has not been transcribed yet" | This file has no transcript in the project. |
| "has changed since it was transcribed" | The file on disk isn't the one that was transcribed. |
| "was transcribed with a different language" | The named setting differs from the transcript's. It can also name **model**, **speakers** or **vocabulary**, or several of them. |
| "was transcribed for a different request" | Something else about the request differs. |
| "is already transcribed, and Transcribe again was asked for" | You ticked [Transcribe again](#transcribe-again). |
| "could not be read, so it cannot be transcribed" | The media file couldn't be read. |

## Split the words by speaker

Tick **Speakers:** ("split by speaker, coloured in Subtitles") to have AssemblyAI label who says what. It's off by default and adds $0.02 an hour to the price.

A change of speaker then always starts a new cue or page. In the [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) style, each speaker's cues take their own colour.

Speakers are counted separately for each media file. A speaker is a label within one file, so the same person in two files can come back as two different speakers.

## Add names and jargon

Type the words you expect into **Vocabulary:**, separated by commas: product names, people, identifiers. AssemblyAI then spells them your way. The field starts empty, and its placeholder reads "names and jargon, separated by commas".

Blank entries and repeats are dropped, keeping the first spelling. The list stops at 1,000 terms, which is AssemblyAI's limit, and it's cut from the end, so put the terms that matter most first. When the limit cuts your list, the note reads "Vocabulary was capped at 1000 terms (AssemblyAI's limit); N were given."

## Choose a language

**Language:** opens on **Detect automatically**, which leaves the language to AssemblyAI. The [result](#what-the-result-says) then tells you what it found.

You can also name one: English, English (Australia), English (United Kingdom), English (United States), Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Arabic, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, Hebrew, Hindi, Japanese, Chinese, Norwegian, Swedish, Turkish or Vietnamese. That list is what AssemblyAI published on 2026-09-17, so it can fall behind.

## Reuse a transcript

Each media file's transcript is kept in the project package, every word as AssemblyAI sent it. A later run that wants the same transcript uses it, with no upload, no request and no cost.

A transcript is reused when all of these match:

- **The file:** its size, modified time and duration, and whether it has audio. Change the file, or relink to a different one, and it's transcribed again.
- **The model** Frame Job asks for.
- **The language:** **Detect automatically** and a named language count as different, as do two named languages.
- **Speakers:** on or off.
- **Vocabulary:** the same terms in the same order.

The caption style and the looks don't count, so [restyling](/captions/restyle-captions/) never uploads. Your region doesn't count either, so changing it uploads nothing again.

A transcript made for [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) serves captions too, as long as those settings match.

The transcript belongs to the media entry, not the file on disk. Two media entries over the same file are uploaded and billed separately.

## Transcribe again

Tick **Transcribe again:** ("ignore any cached transcript") to throw away what's kept and ask AssemblyAI again. It's off by default. Each file goes up in full and is billed again, and the summary line shows that price.

Frame Job won't do this for a file with a [pending delete](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#a-pending-delete-holds-a-file-back) until the delete goes through.

## Generate with no key

With no key set, the note reads "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription.", **Generate** is greyed, and resting the pointer on it shows the same sentence. Saving a key in Settings turns **Generate** on with the sheet still open.

The exception is work you've already paid for. When every file in the run has a current transcript, **Generate** works with no key, and the paragraph at the top changes to "Current cached transcripts will be used without an API key or network request." Ticking **Transcribe again:** ends that, because it needs a new upload.

With a key set the paragraph stays as it is, and the summary line says there's nothing to upload.

## Transcribe an untitled project

You don't have to save first. An untitled project's transcripts stay in a temporary folder and move into the project package on its first save. Close the project without saving and they're gone, so the same files would be paid for again in a new project.

In the rare case that a project has no folder for them at all, **Generate** is greyed and the note reads "This project has nowhere to keep its transcript cache, so it cannot be transcribed with AssemblyAI. Save it first."

## What the result says

While a run goes, the card's detail line shows the stage for each file: "Extracting", "Uploading" with the megabytes sent, "Submitting", "Waiting for AssemblyAI" with the seconds so far, and "Saving".

A run with nothing to report closes the sheet by itself. If there is something, the card stays open with **Close**, and these lines can join the usual count of captions added:

| The card says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "“interview.mov”: detected Spanish (97% confidence)." | With **Detect automatically**, the language AssemblyAI found in each file it just transcribed, and how sure it was. The figure is left out if AssemblyAI gave none. |
| "“interview.mov” was transcribed with universal-2, not universal-3-5-pro." | AssemblyAI used the fallback model. |
| "The transcript of “interview.mov” could not be kept in the project for reuse." | The captions are fine, but a later run may upload and bill this file again. |
| "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of…" | See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#what-the-result-warns-about). |

## When a file fails

One file's failure doesn't end a run. Its clips are listed with the reason, and captions from the other files are still placed. If every file fails, nothing is placed and the card shows why.

Two things end a run early, and neither places anything: choosing **Cancel**, and a key AssemblyAI refuses, because every later upload would fail the same way. Files that had already finished stay in the project, so a later run doesn't pay for them again.

| The reason reads | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| "No network connection" | Frame Job couldn't reach AssemblyAI. |
| "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" | AssemblyAI turned the key down, and the run stops there. Try **Verify** in [Settings](/captions/assemblyai-key/#verify). |
| "AssemblyAI answered 500" | AssemblyAI had a problem of its own. The number varies. |
| "AssemblyAI did not finish the transcript in the time allowed." | Frame Job waits at least 5 minutes for a transcript, and longer for audio over about 4 hours. |
| "“name” is longer than AssemblyAI's 10-hour limit for one file." | Nothing was sent for this file. |
| "AssemblyAI may have created a transcript, but Frame Job could not recover its ID…" | The answer to the request was lost. Check your AssemblyAI dashboard before you try again, because a retry could be billed and the transcript may still be there. |
| AssemblyAI's own sentence | AssemblyAI turned the request down, for a reason such as your account's balance, and Frame Job passes on its words. |

A failed upload is tried once more, unless AssemblyAI turned it down outright. While waiting, Frame Job checks on the transcript every 3 seconds and rides out up to 3 failed checks in a row. It never follows a redirect, so your key can't reach another host, and the run reports that instead.

## Filler words stay out of captions

AssemblyAI's words include fillers, and captions leave them out, so a caption reads the same whether or not its transcript has them. The sheet's preview leaves them out too.

The words left out are um, uh, hmm, mhm, uh-huh, ah, huh, hm, m, er and erm, in any case and with any punctuation at their edges. The kept transcript still has them, which is what lets [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) find them later.

## With an agent

`transcribe` never picks this engine by itself: an agent has to ask for AssemblyAI on each call, whatever the sheet last chose. It can pass any language code, and one AssemblyAI doesn't support comes back as AssemblyAI's own sentence after the upload.

The built-in [Assistant](/assistant/privacy/) can't use this engine at all. Your audio leaves the Mac only when you choose that in the sheet, with the price in front of you.

See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

## Related

- [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/)
- [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/)
- [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/)
- [Transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/)
- [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/)

---
title: "What goes to AssemblyAI"
description: What leaves your Mac when you transcribe with AssemblyAI, what you're billed for, how the transcript is deleted afterwards, and what happens when a delete doesn't land.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

When you transcribe with AssemblyAI, the sound of your files leaves your Mac, and only after you press **Generate**. Frame Job then asks AssemblyAI to delete its transcript as soon as it has the words. Captions made [on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/) never leave it.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Generate Captions…', 'Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…']}
  where="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription ▸ ⓘ"
  tools="transcribe"
  needs="Your own AssemblyAI key."
/>

## What is uploaded and billed

| Goes to AssemblyAI | Stays on your Mac |
| --- | --- |
| The whole audio of each media file behind the chosen clips | The video |
| Your **Vocabulary:** terms, and the language and **Speakers:** settings | The project and the rest of its media |

The audio goes up as 16 kHz mono FLAC, about half the size of a WAV with the same samples. If the FLAC can't be written, a WAV goes up instead. Frame Job removes its temporary copy from your Mac when the upload ends, whether or not it worked.

It's the whole file, not only the parts your clips use, and AssemblyAI bills for the whole file. A two-hour recording you use 30 seconds of costs two hours, about $0.42 at the rate [Frame Job shows](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#the-price-before-you-press-generate). A file over 10 hours is turned down before anything is sent.

The audio goes to the [region](/captions/assemblyai-key/#region) set in Settings, and the sheet names that region before you press **Generate**. **Transcribe** in [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) sends audio in the same way.

:::caution
A recording of someone else goes to a third party here. Get their say-so first, or use **On this Mac**.
:::

## The transcript is deleted after reading

Each file's round trip runs in this order: upload, transcribe, read the words back, save them in the project package, then ask AssemblyAI to delete its transcript. You don't have to do anything. Each delete request has 5 seconds to answer.

Frame Job also asks for the delete when a transcript fails, runs out of time or can't be used, and when you choose **Cancel** while AssemblyAI is working.

A copy of the words stays in your [project package](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#reuse-a-transcript). That copy is what makes later runs free.

If AssemblyAI doesn't confirm the delete, [the result says so](#what-the-result-warns-about).

## Unconfirmed deletes are retried

An unconfirmed delete is retried at the start of the next AssemblyAI run in the same project that has a key. Every delete the project is owed is retried then, whichever files the run is about.

The retry uses the key and region set at that later run, so it can only work with a key for the account and region that made the upload. The two regions don't share transcripts. If you've changed either since, set it back for a run.

With no key set when that next run starts, nothing is sent, and the delete waits for a run that has one.

## A pending delete holds a file back

While a delete is pending, Frame Job won't upload that file again, because the kept transcript is its only record of what's still owed. If that file's kept transcript still matches the run, it's used as normal. If the file needs a new upload, or you ticked [Transcribe again](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#transcribe-again), it waits:

- The summary line counts it apart, as "1 file waiting on an earlier delete", and leaves it out of the price.
- Resting the pointer on the summary gives its price: "It is waiting on an earlier delete and will not be uploaded in this run — about $0.42 more if it does."

The hover line says "if it does" because the retry happens first. If the delete goes through at the start of the run, the file uploads in that same run. If it doesn't, the file isn't uploaded, and its clips are listed with the reason "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting its earlier transcript, so it was not uploaded again; the next run with an API key retries the delete".

## What the result warns about

These lines appear on the sheet's result card, with the file's name in place of "name".

| The card says | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of “name”; it will be retried at the next run with an API key." | Nothing. Run AssemblyAI again in this project when you next need it, with the same account and region. |
| "…It was not uploaded again in this run." | Added to the line above when the delete held the file back. |
| "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of “name”; cleanup was deferred because no API key is set. Its deletion ID is retained in the project; a later run with a key for the originating account and region will retry deletion only if that ID is safe to send." | Set the key for that account and region, then run again in this project. |
| "AssemblyAI has not confirmed deleting the transcript of “name”. Its transcript could not be saved in the project, so Frame Job cannot retry deleting it automatically. Delete it in your AssemblyAI dashboard." | Frame Job has no record to retry from. Choose [Account Page](/captions/assemblyai-key/#open-your-assemblyai-account) in Settings and delete it there. |

:::caution
In an [untitled project](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#transcribe-an-untitled-project), the record of a pending delete lives in a temporary folder. If you never save the project, that record is lost and Frame Job can't retry. Save the project, or delete the transcript in your AssemblyAI dashboard.
:::

## Related

- [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/)
- [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/)
- [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/)
- [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/)

---
title: "Your AssemblyAI key"
description: Save, check and remove the AssemblyAI key that turns on cloud captions and Remove Filler Words, choose your region, and see where the key is kept.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Your AssemblyAI key turns on cloud transcription, and AssemblyAI bills your account directly. It lives in Settings, so it's the same for every project, and you can set it with no project open. For how keys work across Frame Job, see [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/).

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
  keys="⌘,"
  where="Settings ▸ Transcription"
  needs="An AssemblyAI account."
/>

<Shot
  name="02-settings.window"
  alt="The Settings window. Under the Transcription heading, with its info button, are an AssemblyAI API key field reading Paste your key, a Region pop-up set to United States, the line No API key is set, and the buttons Save, Remove, Verify and Account Page. Remove and Verify are greyed."
/>

## Save your AssemblyAI key

<Steps>

1. Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>) and find **Transcription**.

2. Choose **Account Page** to get a key from your AssemblyAI dashboard.

3. Paste the key into **AssemblyAI API key:**.

4. Choose **Save**, or press <kbd>Return</kbd>.

5. Choose [**Verify**](#check-the-key) to check that it works.

</Steps>

The line under the controls says "Key saved.", and the field empties. From then on the field shows a fixed row of dots, the same length whatever your key is. The key itself never goes back in the field, so it can't be read or copied out of the window.

With no key anywhere, the line reads "No API key is set." in ordinary grey. That's a state, not a problem. **Save** with an empty field beeps and does nothing.

If the key file can't be written, the line reads "The API key could not be saved:" and gives the reason. The field is emptied anyway, so paste the key again once it's fixed.

## Check the key

**Verify** makes AssemblyAI's cheapest signed-in request, with your key and region, to see if the key works. It doesn't transcribe or bill anything.

It checks the key a real run would use: the one typed in the field, even if you haven't saved it, then the saved key, then [the environment's](#use-a-key-from-the-environment). A typed key is only checked, so choose **Save** as well to keep it.

| The line says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Checking…" | The request is on its way. |
| "Key accepted" | AssemblyAI accepted the key in this region. |
| "Settings changed since this check began. Verify again." | You changed the key or the region during the check, so its answer no longer applies. |
| AssemblyAI's message, such as "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" | The check failed, and the message says why. "No network connection" is another. |

**Verify** is greyed when there's no key at all, and while a check of the same key and region is running.

## Choose a region

**Region:** chooses the AssemblyAI data centre your audio goes to: **United States**, the default, or **European Union**. It's saved as soon as you pick it, and an open sheet updates straight away. The Generate Captions and Remove Filler Words sheets name the region before you upload.

A transcript made in one region can't be seen from the other, so pick the region your account uses. [A pending delete](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/#unconfirmed-deletes-are-retried) only succeeds in the region it was made in.

Changing the region doesn't upload anything again. Transcripts already kept in a project stay usable.

## Open your AssemblyAI account

**Account Page** opens your AssemblyAI dashboard in your browser, at `https://www.assemblyai.com/dashboard`. That's where you get a key and see what you've spent.

## Remove the key

**Remove** deletes the saved key and says "Key removed." It's greyed unless a key is saved.

If the removal fails, the key stays saved and the line says why.

## Where the key is kept

The key is saved in a file only your account can read, not in the Keychain:

`~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/assemblyai-key`

The file's mode is `0600`, and it sits beside `anthropic-key`, the [Assistant](/assistant/set-up/)'s key. Any program running as you can read it, so treat that file like a password. The key is never passed on the command line.

## Use a key from the environment

If no key is saved, Frame Job also accepts one from the `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` environment variable, which is useful when you launch it from a terminal.

- A saved key always wins over the variable.
- An empty variable counts as no key.
- **Verify** checks the variable's key when nothing is typed or saved.
- **Remove** stays greyed, because nothing is saved.

See [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/).

## What the key turns on

| Feature | Without a key |
| --- | --- |
| The **AssemblyAI** engine of [Generate Captions](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) | **Generate** is greyed, [unless every file is already transcribed](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#generate-with-no-key). |
| [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/), which finds fillers only through AssemblyAI | The menu item reads **Remove Filler Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)**. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/) for what works without one. |

Captions made [on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/) need no key.

Saving or removing a key, or changing the region, reaches an open Generate Captions sheet straight away, so **Generate** can come on without reopening it.

## What the info button says

The ⓘ beside the **Transcription** heading explains three things:

- **What leaves your Mac.** The audio of the files you're captioning is uploaded, transcribed, read back and then deleted from AssemblyAI. A delete that didn't land is retried at the start of the next run. Nothing is uploaded until you press **Generate**, and captions made on this Mac never leave it.
- **The rate.** AssemblyAI's published rate as Frame Job last read it: $0.21 an hour of audio, and $0.02 more with **Speakers:** on, read on 2026-09-17.
- **The key.** It's kept in a file only you can read and is never shown again once it's saved.

[What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/) has the full story.

## Only a person sets the key

No agent tool can read or change the key or the region, and an agent can't pass a key of its own. Only you set them, here. An agent's `transcribe` call uses the key you've saved, and with none it stops with the same "No AssemblyAI API key is set." sentence.

- [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>
